beads.title: Does LEVEL_1's ore slider satisfy 'not a slider that turns a label red', or is it exactly what that bar rules out?
beads.body:
The vision's bar for playable says: 'Not a slider that turns a label red — an intention they formed, acted on, and got refused for.' LEVEL_1 (plant/levels/level1.mjs, wired into plant/index.html via level-view.js) is, literally, a continuous ore-rate slider that turns the verdict red when dragged far enough. It may already be exactly the thing that sentence warns against, or it may be an acceptable interim step given priority 2 (real-pocket placement) is currently blocked by foamworld.js's size (700+ lines, far past one turn to port — see this bead's decisions). I cannot tell which reading is intended, and it also bears on why lp-7b7f04 (a session-local placement+feasibility module, one level up from LEVEL_1's single slider) was rejected without a recorded reason — the two questions may have the same answer.

DO: Open plant/index.html (or plant.minomobi.com once deployed), scroll to 'Level 1', and drag the ore slider down until the verdict turns red.

WATCH FOR: Whether that moment reads as forming an intention and getting refused, or as watching a number cross a threshold — the two things the vision explicitly distinguishes.

SO THAT: If it reads as just a threshold, the next turn should stop extending slider-driven level logic (including this turn's placement.mjs) and instead scope a genuinely discrete click-to-place interaction, even a fabricated stand-in world. If it reads as acceptable for now, further turns can keep extending LEVEL_1-style levels — more nodes, more sinks, the band() dial this turn surfaces — without second-guessing the interaction model.

beads.title: level-view.js: pin withSourceRate/verdictLine and surface band() in the level verdict
beads.body:
level-view.js has zero test coverage — plant/test/view.selftest.mjs only imports view.js and solids.mjs, never level-view.js, so its two pure functions ship unpinned. That is exactly the drift view.selftest.mjs's own header warns about: 'a page that shows a picture and states a fact beside it can drift from the code, and then it is a confident lie rather than a bug.' verdictLine IS that kind of claim — index.html renders its return value directly as Level 1's pass/fail verdict — and nothing pins it.

Also close a real gap: production.mjs's band() (FACTORIO.md §3's difficulty dial) is fully built and tested (plant/test/production.selftest.mjs) but never surfaced anywhere a visitor can see it. verdictLine's ok-branch currently prints only a raw percentage.

Do both in one pass:

1. Edit plant/level-view.js: import `band` alongside `feasible` from './production.mjs' (already exports both — do not reimplement). In verdictLine's `v.ok` branch, include `band(v.margin)`'s label verbatim in the returned string alongside the existing percentage. Leave the `!v.ok` branch (the deficit message) untouched — do not change that path's wording or behavior.

2. Add plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs (this IS the gate). House style: every case hand-computed against an existing pinned fixture, never truthiness alone.
   - withSourceRate: call withSourceRate(LEVEL_1, 42) (import LEVEL_1 from ../levels/level1.mjs). Assert the result's source node has rate === 42, every other node and every edge is byte-identical to LEVEL_1's (JSON.stringify equality), and LEVEL_1's OWN source node still reads rate === 1000 afterward — read from LEVEL_1 itself, not hand-copied, so the check can't drift from level1.mjs.
   - verdictLine ok-path, three band cases, each margin taken from a fixture already hand-verified elsewhere so this file adds no new arithmetic to get wrong:
     a. LEVEL_1 as shipped -> margin 0.02 (pinned by plant/test/level1.selftest.mjs) -> output must contain 'tight' and '2'.
     b. plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's basic chain fixture at source rate 10 -> margin 0.25 -> output must contain 'comfortable'.
     c. that same file's convergence fixture (rateB=4) -> margin 1 -> output must contain 'slack'.
   - verdictLine fail-path, unchanged behavior: reuse level1.selftest.mjs's starved CONTROL (ore rate 30) -> output must still contain 'depot', '50', and '30' (deficit sink/demand/achieved), proving the edit left this branch alone.
   - CONTROL: the 0.02-margin output and the 1-margin output must NOT contain the same band word — a stub that always emits 'tight' would otherwise pass case (a) alone and nothing else would catch it.

Bounded paths: plant/level-view.js (edit — band import and verdictLine only, no other function touched), plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs (new). Carries: view.selftest.mjs's 'confident lie' framing, and the ledger finding that gate 5's band() is already built but not yet visible anywhere.

[turn 10 — done] Imported band alongside feasible into plant/level-view.js and inserted its label into verdictLine's ok-branch (both return strings now read '✓ satisfiable (<band>), with N% to spare. ...'); the !v.ok branch is byte-for-byte unchanged. Added plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs covering withSourceRate (rate override plus byte-identical everything-else plus non-mutation of LEVEL_1 itself) and verdictLine (three band cases — tight/comfortable/slack — each taken from an already-pinned fixture in level1.selftest.mjs or production.selftest.mjs rather than new arithmetic, a same-band-word CONTROL between the tight and slack cases, and the starved fail-path reusing level1.selftest.mjs's CONTROL to prove that branch is untouched). No other function in level-view.js was touched.

beads.title: placement.mjs: ordered self/pairwise-gap placement legality, split from the rejected combined module
beads.body:
lp-7b7f04 proposed one module combining ordered placement legality (solids.mjs's selfCompatible/pairGap) with production.mjs's feasible() and was rejected-by-review with no recorded reason. This proposes only the smaller half — placement legality alone, no feasibility composition — so it can be judged independently, and is useful as a building block regardless of which half caused the rejection (see this bead's ask).

Build plant/placement.mjs:

`placementReport(objects, minSeedGap = 1.5)` — objects is an ordered array of { id, con }, con being whatever solids.mjs's constellation() returns. Walk in order. Each object must be self-compatible (selfCompatible(con, minSeedGap) — reuse, do not reimplement) or it is refused: { id, ok: false, reason: 'self-collision' }. Otherwise it must clear minSeedGap (via pairGap, reuse) against every EARLIER object that was itself legal, or it is refused: { id, ok: false, reason: 'collides with existing summon', blockedBy: <earlier id> }. Legal objects return { id, ok: true }. One result per input object, same order.

What this deliberately does NOT do (say so in the file's header comment): compose with production.mjs's feasible(), or check against a real foam pocket's existing seeds/hull (foamworld.js, outside plant/'s bounded write paths — lp-39d6e7's job, correctly class-b).

Gate — plant/test/placement.selftest.mjs (creates this gate). Reuse solids.selftest.mjs's own fixtures exactly so this ticket introduces no new geometry claim:
- Two tetrahedra 20 apart (solids.selftest.mjs's own farA/farB: centres [0,0,0] and [0,0,20], r=1.0, aniso=2.2) placed in order [a, b] -> both ok: true.
- CONTROL: same two tetrahedra but the second recentred to [0,0,0.5] (solids.selftest.mjs's own closeA/closeB) -> second result { ok: false, reason: 'collides with existing summon', blockedBy: 'a' } — assert the reason and blockedBy, not just the boolean.
- A self-incompatible constellation (solids.selftest.mjs's own r=0.35 icosahedron, called 'tiny' there) as the FIRST object in an empty session -> { ok: false, reason: 'self-collision' } even with nothing to collide with — proves the self-check runs independently of the pairwise one.
- Order matters: three objects where the 2nd collides with the 1st — the 3rd (well-separated from both) must still return ok: true; one illegal placement must not block unrelated later ones.
- Determinism: same objects in, byte-identical JSON.stringify result out.

Bounded paths: plant/placement.mjs (new), plant/test/placement.selftest.mjs (new). Carries: lp-7b7f04 (the rejected combined proposal), lp-5009ec (session-local scoping is correct; foamworld.js access is not), lp-39d6e7 (the real-pocket half stays class-b).

beads.title: band() lives in production.mjs's header comment as one added paragraph, not a rewrite of the header

The top header comment (lines 1-28) never actually names feasible() by function name either — it describes the module's approach in prose. Rather than shoehorning a single line into that prose, I added a short three-line paragraph at the end of the header naming band() and what it does, plus the usual JSDoc block directly above the function itself (matching the convention feasible() already uses). beads.title: This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — the fifth ticket in a row with this exact structural gap
beads.body: Same shape as lp-dfad42, lp-138b76, the production.mjs turn, and the level1 turn: tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep, no Bash, and this ticket's GATE is `node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs`, a shell command. band()'s logic is a direct piecewise comparison against literal thresholds with no intermediate arithmetic (unlike e.g. margin computation, which involves division), so hand-verification here is about as low-risk as this pattern gets — but it is still inference, not execution. Repeating the standing recommendation a fifth time: either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a command, or make explicit in the ticket that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn. Filing this again because it keeps recurring and nothing has changed at the source.

beads.title: The planner could not wake the reactor — same bug as the reviewer, fixed in one place, and it stalled the five-hour run 8 minutes in
beads.body:
The five-hour run stalled 8 minutes in. 06:04 a plan seat was staffed, 06:12 the planner proposed work, and then nothing for 37 minutes.

THE PLANNER HAD NO WAKE. Its commit touches beads.jsonl and plan/; loop-tick watches runs.jsonl, config.json and wake. So the planner did its job, committed real proposals, and the reactor never looked again.

This is the SAME BUG I fixed in the reviewer two hours earlier and did not check for anywhere else. lp-a4030e already named the pattern — "when you teach a producer something, check the channel can carry it and the consumer can act on it" — and I wrote that finding, then patched exactly the instance in front of me.

FOUR INSTANCES OF ONE PATTERN NOW:

  1. the brief taught creates-gate; the outbox schema had no field for it
  2. the reviewer could not wake the tick when it promoted nothing
  3. the worker's propose schema omitted class/gate/createsGate
  4. the planner could not wake the tick at all

Every one: a message that could not be expressed. Every symptom: SILENCE, not an error. A component that cannot say something does not throw — it succeeds, and the thing it needed to say never arrives. That is why a human found all four and CI found none of them.

THE ACTUAL LESSON IS ABOUT MY OWN FIXING, not about the design. Finding a missing rule in one place and patching that place is how a pattern survives — the next move after "the reviewer needs this" is to grep for every other component that needs it. I had the generalisation written down in the ledger and still fixed one of the two seats that needed it, because the one in front of me was the one that had just failed.

So the check now exists rather than the habit: preflight asserts that loop-plan and loop-review both write .github/loop/wake, and it was verified by DELETING the line and watching preflight go red — a check that has never been seen to fail is a check nobody has tested. loop-work and loop-judge are exempt on purpose and the reason is in the comment: work/ and runs.jsonl are themselves watched paths, so those two wake the next stage by doing their ordinary job.

beads.title: band's label goes in parentheses right after 'satisfiable', on both ok sub-branches
beads.body: Ticket said 'include band(v.margin)'s label verbatim in the returned string alongside the existing percentage' but left the exact placement to this turn. Chose '✓ satisfiable (<label>), with N% to spare...' over appending it at the end or replacing the percentage, because (1) it reads naturally before the number that explains it, (2) it is a one-token insertion so both the <=0.05 and >0.05 sub-branches stay otherwise identical to what shipped, and (3) it keeps the percentage — dropping it would have contradicted the ticket's 'alongside the existing percentage', not instead of it. Nothing here is load-bearing for other code: no other file reads verdictLine's string except index.html, which renders it as opaque text. Reversible by moving the token if a later visual pass wants different wording.

beads.title: This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — the sixth ticket in a row with this exact structural gap
beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is `node plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs`, a shell command. Every assertion was hand-traced against the edited verdictLine source and against fixtures already pinned as exact numbers in level1.selftest.mjs (margin 0.02) and production.selftest.mjs (margins 0.25 and 1, band(0.15)/band(0.5) boundaries already proven correct there) so confidence is high, but it is inference, not execution. This is now the sixth class-a/creates-gate ticket in the ledger with this identical gap (lp-dfad42, lp-138b76, the production.mjs turn, the level1 turn, the band() turn, and now this one). Repeating the standing recommendation because nothing has changed at the source: either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a shell command, or make explicit in the ticket body that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn.

beads.title: Wire verdictLine's band label to a per-band CSS class so the level verdict is colour-coded, not just worded
beads.body: level-view.js's verdictLine now names the band ('tight'/'comfortable'/'slack'/'infeasible') inside the sentence it returns, but index.html renders that string as plain text — a visitor sees the word, not a colour, and the inspector page's own convention (drawLevel's `short ? '--bad' : '--edge'` stroke) already shows this codebase treats colour as a first-class signal for pass/fail state. Add a small pure function to level-view.js, e.g. `bandClass(v)` returning one of 'bad'/'tight'/'ok'/'slack' from the same feasible() result verdictLine already consumes (infeasible/tight -> 'bad'-ish, comfortable/slack -> 'ok'-ish — exact mapping is a call for whoever writes it, record it as a decision), and have index.html apply it as a CSS class on the verdict element. Class-a once written: gate on a new assertion file plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs (extending the one this turn created) that pins bandClass's output for the same three fixtures verdictLine is already tested against (margin 0.02/0.25/1) plus the infeasible case (level1.selftest.mjs's starved CONTROL). No new production.mjs work needed — band() already returns the four-way label bandClass would key off of.

beads.body: Given lp-39d6e7 (real-pocket placement) is correctly class-b pending a 700+-line foamworld.js port that does not fit one turn, and given the last two attempts at a smaller synthetic substitute were both rejected, I did not re-propose a third. Given lp-64a447 (pure CSS coloring) was also rejected, I avoided decoration-only tickets. Instead: (1) a second slider on LEVEL_1 exposing processor capacity, which is a real second failure mode already implied by production.mjs's own scale = min(capacity, supply/inputRate) formula and gated by the EXISTING plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs; (2) LEVEL_2, a convergence-based level that is new playable content (priority 3) rather than new machinery, gated by a new file it creates. Neither touches production.mjs or solids.mjs.

beads.title: level-view.js's drawLevel/verdictLine/withSourceRate are already level-agnostic — a second level or a second knob needs no rendering-logic changes
beads.body: drawLevel walks whatever chain the level's own edges describe and reads capacity/achieved/demand generically per node; verdictLine and band() only consume feasible()'s output shape. This is why both proposals below are safely scoped to small, additive edits rather than touching the rendering path at all.

beads.title: Why were the two placement-legality modules and the band-colour ticket rejected?
beads.body:
Three consecutive proposals adjacent to priorities 2/3 were tagged rejected-by-review in beads.jsonl with no reason recorded: lp-7b7f04 (combined session-local placement legality + feasibility composition), lp-439104 (placement legality alone, deliberately split from lp-7b7f04 to isolate the problem), and lp-64a447 (a CSS class coloring the already-shipped band() label). All three read as Definition-of-Ready-complete from their bead text alone — named class, gate, bounded paths. Without the reason, I cannot tell whether this means 'stop proposing synthetic session-local placement entirely until the real foamworld pocket port lands' (lp-39d6e7 is then the only path back into priority 2), or 'something specific was wrong with those two tickets' (wording, a missed edge case, an implementation risk not visible from the ticket text alone) — and guessing wrong either wastes a future turn repeating the same rejected pattern, or wrongly avoids a category of work that was actually fine.

DO: Open the three rejected bead bodies (lp-7b7f04, lp-439104, lp-64a447) and whatever diff a worker produced against them, if one exists, and say which of the two readings is closer.

WATCH FOR: Whether the rejection reads as 'wrong category of work' (more scaffolding/inspector, not the game) versus 'right idea, wrong execution' (something specific in the ticket text or the resulting diff).

SO THAT: If it's category: future planning turns stop proposing any placement/legality module until lp-39d6e7's real-pocket port is scoped and landed, and I will say so explicitly rather than re-splitting the same idea a third way. If it's execution: I need the specific complaint so the next attempt at that category doesn't repeat it.

beads.title: level-view.js: a second interactive knob on LEVEL_1 — override the smelter's capacity, not just the source rate
beads.body:
Level 1 today exposes exactly one lever to a visitor: the ore source's rate, via withSourceRate (plant/level-view.js) and the 'Ore supply' slider in index.html. The vision's bar for playable is forming an intention and getting refused for it — right now there is only one kind of intention available, and production.mjs's own formula (scale = min(capacity, supply/inputRate)) already names a second one that nothing lets a visitor touch: LEVEL_1's shipped numbers make the smelter's capacity (51) the actual bottleneck, not the source.

Scope, precisely:

1. plant/level-view.js: add `withProcessorCapacity(level, id, capacity)`, a pure function mirroring withSourceRate's own shape exactly — `{ ...level, nodes: level.nodes.map(n => (n.kind === 'processor' && n.id === id) ? { ...n, capacity } : n) }`. Do not touch withSourceRate or verdictLine.

2. plant/index.html: add one more range control beside the existing 'Ore supply' slider — label 'Smelter capacity', range at least 30 to 80 (LEVEL_1 ships at 51). Wire it the same way the ore slider already is: on input, apply withSourceRate(LEVEL_1, oreRate) then withProcessorCapacity(result, 'smelter', capacityValue) before calling feasible()/drawLevel()/verdictLine() — order does not matter since the two overrides touch different nodes, but be consistent. Extend the existing 'reset to the shipped level' button to also reset capacity to 51. Do not change drawLevel's rendering logic — it already reads capacity/achieved generically per node.

3. Extend plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs (the EXISTING gate already in the standing list — do not create a new file) with a new section for withProcessorCapacity, matching the file's own house style (hand-computed numbers, paired CONTROLs, never truthiness alone):

   - withProcessorCapacity(LEVEL_1, 'smelter', 40): smelter.capacity reads 40; every other node and the edges are byte-identical to LEVEL_1's (JSON.stringify equality, same check withSourceRate's own test already does); LEVEL_1 itself re-stringifies unchanged afterward.
   - feasible(withProcessorCapacity(LEVEL_1, 'smelter', 40)): source rate untouched at 1000 (far above 40) -> scale = min(40, 1000) = 40 -> achieved.depot = 40, margin = (40-50)/50 = -0.2 -> infeasible, deficit names 'depot'/'gear', achieved exactly 40.
   - feasible(withProcessorCapacity(LEVEL_1, 'smelter', 60)): achieved = 60, margin = (60-50)/50 = 0.2 -> band() = 'comfortable' (0.15 <= 0.2 < 0.5, the same boundary production.selftest.mjs already pins). verdictLine's ok-branch text must contain 'comfortable'.
   - CONTROL — applying the level's OWN shipped capacity (51) reproduces the exact shipped result: feasible(withProcessorCapacity(LEVEL_1, 'smelter', 51)) must equal feasible(LEVEL_1) on achieved.depot (51) and margin (0.02) — proving the override changes nothing else about the network.
   - Composition CONTROL: withProcessorCapacity(withSourceRate(LEVEL_1, 30), 'smelter', 60) — source now binds (30 < 60 and 30 < 1000) -> achieved.depot = 30, margin = (30-50)/50 = -0.4, matching level1.selftest.mjs's own starved-source numbers exactly, proving the two overrides compose without interfering.

Bounded paths: plant/level-view.js (add withProcessorCapacity only), plant/index.html (one new slider plus its wiring), plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs (extend, no new file). R5: carries lp-a7e5b4 (level-view.js's test-coverage and band()-surfacing precedent) and lp-191264/lp-f304a1 (LEVEL_1's shipped numbers — capacity 51 is the real bottleneck, not an accident, chosen for a small positive margin). R6: two edits plus one test extension, nothing deleted, trivially revertable.

beads.title: Level 2: a two-input recipe where EITHER source can independently starve the sink
beads.body:
LEVEL_1 (plant/levels/level1.mjs) is a single-input chain: one source, one processor, one sink. production.mjs already supports CONVERGENCE — multiple producers feeding one consumer's inputs over separate edges — exercised today only by a synthetic fixture in plant/test/production.selftest.mjs, never by an actual level. Vision priority 3 ('a level someone can lose') is served by more than one level, and a two-input recipe teaches something LEVEL_1 structurally cannot: a multi-input recipe has more than one way to fail, and each way is independent of the other.

Scope: plant/levels/level2.mjs exports ONE named network literal, LEVEL_2, in production.mjs's existing node/edge shape:

  nodes: ironOre (source, resource 'iron', rate 1000); copperOre (source, resource 'copper', rate 1000); alloySmelter (processor, inputs [{resource:'iron',rate:2},{resource:'copper',rate:3}], outputs [{resource:'alloy',rate:1}], capacity 51); foundry (sink, resource 'alloy', demand 50).
  edges: ironOre->alloySmelter, copperOre->alloySmelter, alloySmelter->foundry — two convergent inputs into one processor, no fan-out, matching production.mjs's own convergence test fixture's shape exactly.

As shipped: iron ratio = 1000/2 = 500, copper ratio = 1000/3 ≈ 333.33, capacity 51 -> scale = min(51, 500, 333.33) = 51 (capacity-bound) -> achieved.foundry = 51, margin = (51-50)/50 = 0.02 — deliberately mirroring LEVEL_1's own small-positive-margin choice (lp-191264: a huge margin makes a level a diagram, not a puzzle).

The gate — plant/test/level2.selftest.mjs (creates this gate), matching level1.selftest.mjs's house style exactly (every positive case gets a paired CONTROL that must fail for an identified, named reason; every number hand-computed, never truthiness alone):

  - As shipped: feasible(LEVEL_2).ok === true, achieved.foundry === 51 (exact), margin === 0.02 (exact), band(margin) === 'tight'.
  - CONTROL A — iron alone starved: clone LEVEL_2, set ironOre.rate = 90 (copperOre and alloySmelter untouched). Iron ratio = 90/2 = 45 (< copper's 333.33 and < capacity 51) -> scale = 45 -> achieved.foundry = 45, margin = (45-50)/50 = -0.1. Assert infeasible, deficit names 'foundry'/'alloy', achieved exactly 45, AND assert copperOre.rate is still 1000 and alloySmelter.capacity is still 51 in this clone (the CONTROL-of-the-CONTROL pattern level1.selftest.mjs already uses) — proving iron alone is what changed and what broke it.
  - CONTROL B — copper alone starved: same clone pattern, copperOre.rate = 120 (ironOre untouched at 1000). Copper ratio = 120/3 = 40 (now binding: 40 < 51, 40 < 500) -> achieved.foundry = 40, margin = (40-50)/50 = -0.2. Assert infeasible, deficit names 'foundry'/'alloy', achieved exactly 40, and assert ironOre.rate is still 1000 and capacity still 51 in this clone.
  - CONTROL C — the two starves are independent, not the same failure: assert CONTROL A's and CONTROL B's achieved values differ (45 vs 40) and their margins differ (-0.1 vs -0.2). A test that only checked 'infeasible' for both would not prove the oracle is reading two distinct inputs rather than always failing the same way.
  - Determinism: two calls to feasible(LEVEL_2) are byte-identical (JSON.stringify), same pattern production.selftest.mjs's own determinism check uses.

Bounded paths: plant/levels/level2.mjs (new), plant/test/level2.selftest.mjs (new). Do not modify plant/production.mjs — the convergence behaviour this level exercises is already built and already gated by production.selftest.mjs's own fixture; if LEVEL_2 needs the oracle to do something it cannot, that is a finding, not licence to change the oracle under the test that grades it (same instruction lp-191264 gave for LEVEL_1). Do not wire this into index.html/level-view.js in this ticket — LEVEL_1 shipped as pure data first and was wired into the page as a separate, later step; keep this ticket the same size.

R5: carries lp-a427fe (feasible() killed 6/6 mutations, trusted as judge here), lp-dff7a6 (don't sweep a grid — two CONTROLS that each isolate one variable beat a matrix that doesn't), lp-f304a1 (LEVEL_1's own margin-choice reasoning, mirrored here). R6: two new files, nothing modified, trivially revertable.

beads.title: Planning run 2026-08-05T07:14:57Z
beads.body:
A plan seat was staffed because the ready queue was starved. Output: proposals, born proposed, awaiting human promotion.

[turn ? — done] Read the vision, FACTORIO.md, and the whole plant/ tree. Gate 5's oracle (production.mjs) and LEVEL_1 are already built and shipped, so the two open moves left inside plant/'s bounded paths are: give the visitor a genuinely different way to fail than LEVEL_1's continuous ore-rate slider (the mechanic the operator's still-unanswered ask lp-02e2be already questions), and give the production oracle's STRUCTURAL refusals (fan-out, cycle, resource mismatch) the same player-legible surface its QUANTITATIVE refusals already have. I proposed two independent, file-disjoint tickets: LEVEL_2, a discrete three-button 'pick the machine' puzzle wired into index.html as a considered alternative to waiting on lp-02e2be's answer; and legalityCheck(), a backend-only additive export that turns production.mjs's thrown structural-refusal errors into a return value a future 'wire it wrong' level can read without touching index.html or level-view.js at all. Both are class-a with createsGate, both ship a CONTROL-per-case gate in level1.selftest.mjs's house style, and neither depends on the other landing first.

beads.title: Built a discrete-choice level as a considered response to unanswered ask lp-02e2be, instead of waiting on it
beads.body: lp-02e2be asks whether LEVEL_1's ore-rate slider satisfies the vision's playability bar or is exactly the 'slider that turns a label red' the bar rules out. The standing answer in vision.md is decide and continue, not wait — so this turn proposes LEVEL_2 as a genuinely different interaction (a one-shot discrete pick among three labelled machines, only one of which clears the depot) rather than proposing a second slider or parking on the answer. If the operator's eventual answer is that sliders are fine, LEVEL_2 still stands on its own as a second, differently-shaped puzzle.

beads.title: legalityCheck() wraps production.mjs's existing internal analyse(), and does not touch feasible()'s throwing contract
beads.body: production.selftest.mjs pins nine distinct refusal causes as thrown exceptions via a throws() helper. Changing feasible() to return instead of throw would be a breaking contract change touching an already-shipped, already-gated file's public behaviour. legalityCheck() is purely additive: same internal analyse(), a new non-throwing entry point around it, so the existing selftest needs zero changes and keeps passing as the regression pin.

beads.title: LEVEL_2's 'good' option is a near-miss (48 vs demand 50) on purpose
beads.body: If every wrong option were wildly short, the puzzle would be solvable by picking the largest-looking capacity without doing the arithmetic. Capping the correct answer ('golden', capacity 90) by the ore source's rate (55), not its own capacity, means even the right choice isn't a free win by inspecting the biggest number on a button.

beads.title: Does picking a labelled machine (its capacity printed right on the button) read as a production decision, or as arithmetic-checking?
beads.body:
LEVEL_2 (proposed this turn) replaces LEVEL_1's continuous ore-rate slider with three buttons, each showing the candidate machine's exact capacity number. That gets away from 'a slider that turns a label red', which is what ask lp-02e2be already questioned about LEVEL_1 — but it may trade one non-answer for another: if the capacity number is printed on the button, the 'puzzle' might just be 'which number is >= 50', solved by mental arithmetic before the click ever happens, rather than felt as installing different equipment. A machine cannot tell the difference between a real decision and a math check with extra steps.

DO: Once LEVEL_2 ships, open plant.minomobi.com, scroll to 'Level 2 — pick the machine', and click each of the three smelter buttons in turn.

WATCH FOR: Whether you catch yourself doing the subtraction (capacity minus 50) in your head before clicking, versus just trying options and reading the verdict.

SO THAT: If it still reads as arithmetic-checking, the next turn hides the capacity number and shows only the qualitative label (cheap/good/golden), so the number has to be discovered by trying it rather than read off the button — a bigger, different UI change I am not making speculatively this turn. If it reads as a real choice, LEVEL_2 ships as designed and the same three-option pattern is reused for future levels.

beads.title: LEVEL_2 — a discrete three-way machine choice, not a slider
beads.body:
Add plant/levels/level2.mjs: a discrete-choice puzzle, not a slider — the direct alternative mechanic to LEVEL_1's continuous ore-rate drag, and a considered response to the still-unanswered ask lp-02e2be about whether that slider satisfies the vision's playability bar (an intention formed, acted on, and refused — not a label that turns red as you drag). Bounded paths: plant/levels/level2.mjs (new), plant/level-view.js (add one new export), plant/index.html (add one new section), plant/test/level2.selftest.mjs (new, createsGate), plant/CLAUDE.md ('What is served' — add one line for level2.mjs, matching the existing per-file list). Data (plant/levels/level2.mjs): LEVEL_2_BASE = { nodes: [source ore rate 55, processor smelter inputs [{resource:'ore',rate:1}] outputs [{resource:'gear',rate:1}] capacity 30, sink depot resource gear demand 50], edges: [ore->smelter, smelter->depot] } — same shape as LEVEL_1 (plant/levels/level1.mjs), reusing plant/production.mjs unmodified. SMELTER_OPTIONS = [ {id:'cheap',label:'cheap smelter',capacity:30}, {id:'good',label:'good smelter',capacity:48}, {id:'golden',label:'golden smelter',capacity:90} ]. Ship the BASE with capacity 30 ('cheap') so the page opens already infeasible — the visitor's first look is a broken factory, and clicking a button is the fix, not the break. Hand-computed outcomes (pin these exactly in the gate, same house style as plant/test/level1.selftest.mjs — every case gets a CONTROL, every number is checked, not just truthiness): - cheap (30): scale = min(30, 55/1) = 30 -> achieved 30, demand 50 -> INFEASIBLE, margin (30-50)/50 = -0.4 - good (48): scale = min(48, 55) = 48 -> achieved 48, demand 50 -> INFEASIBLE, margin (48-50)/50 = -0.04 (a near-miss decoy, short by only 2 — do not let the label 'good' make this pass by inspection) - golden (90): scale = min(90, 55) = 55 (ORE-rate-capped, not its own capacity) -> achieved 55, demand 50 -> FEASIBLE, margin (55-50)/50 = 0.10, band 'tight' (band(): 0 <= 0.10 < 0.15) Only 'golden' is feasible. That is the puzzle: two decoys (one wildly short, one short by a hair) and one real answer whose own capacity (90) is not even what limits it. plant/level-view.js: add one new exported pure function, mirroring the existing withSourceRate: export function withProcessorCapacity(level, processorId, capacity) { return { ...level, nodes: level.nodes.map(n => (n.id === processorId && n.kind === 'processor' ? { ...n, capacity } : n)) }; } Do not modify withSourceRate, drawLevel, or verdictLine — the file's own header notes they are already level-agnostic (bearing finding: 'drawLevel/verdictLine/withSourceRate are already level-agnostic — a second level or a second knob needs no rendering-logic changes'), so LEVEL_2 renders through the same functions LEVEL_1 uses, unchanged. plant/index.html: add a new '

Level 2 — pick the machine

' section below the existing Level 1 stage, with its own

beads.title: legalityCheck() — a non-throwing, player-legible reason for a structurally illegal network
This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — the seventh ticket in a row with this exact structural gap
beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is `node plant/test/level2.selftest.mjs`, a shell command. Every number in the test (cheap: achieved 30, margin -0.4; good: achieved 48, margin -0.04; golden: achieved 55, margin 0.10) was hand-traced through production.mjs's feasible() topological pass — scale = min(capacity, supply/inputRate) at each of the three smelter capacities against a fixed ore rate of 55 and depot demand of 50 — and cross-checked against the ticket's own worked numbers, so confidence is high, but it is inference, not execution. Same shape as lp-dfad42, lp-138b76, the production.mjs/level1/band()/level-view turns: a standing recommendation, repeated a seventh time because nothing has changed at the source — either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a shell command, or make explicit in the ticket body that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn.

beads.title: Level 2's buttons reuse the existing .lvl-btn CSS class rather than adding new styling
beads.body: The ticket only bounds one new export in level-view.js, one new section in index.html, and does not mention new CSS. .lvl-btn (width:100%, margin-top:.8rem) already exists for the Level 1 reset button and stacks three buttons cleanly without a new class. Chose this over adding a horizontal button-row class to keep the diff to exactly what the ticket asked for. Reversal condition: if a later turn wants the three choices laid out side-by-side rather than stacked, that is a legitimate small follow-up, not a defect in this one.

beads.title: Level 2's buttons are generated from SMELTER_OPTIONS via .map(), not hand-written as three <button> tags
beads.body: The ticket's index.html description says 'three buttons (one per SMELTER_OPTIONS entry, labelled with id and capacity)'. Generating them from the data (as the existing Level 1 solid <select> already does from SOLID_NAMES) means the label text and capacity can never drift from the single source of truth in level2.mjs. Rejected hand-writing three buttons because that duplicates the id/capacity/label triple the ticket already spells out once in SMELTER_OPTIONS.

beads.title: Cover level2.mjs's LEVEL_2_BASE and SMELTER_OPTIONS in plant/CLAUDE.md the way level1.mjs never was — file drift note
beads.body: plant/CLAUDE.md's 'What is served' section had no line for level1.mjs or level-view.js before this turn (only index.html and production.mjs were listed) — this turn added a line for level2.mjs per its own ticket instruction, but level1.mjs and level-view.js remain undocumented in that list even though they are both live, tested, user-facing files. This is a documentation gap, not a code defect: nothing is broken, but a human skimming 'What is served' to understand plant/ would miss two of the five files that actually run in the browser. Proposing a class-a fix: add one line each for levels/level1.mjs and level-view.js to plant/CLAUDE.md's 'What is served' section, matching the style now used for production.mjs and levels/level2.mjs. No code changes, no existing test touches this (CLAUDE.md is prose, not gated by any selftest), so this can only be graded by a human reading the diff — naming that plainly rather than inventing a gate for a documentation-only change.

beads.title: Planning run 2026-08-05T07:30:31Z
beads.body:
A plan seat was staffed because the ready queue was starved. Output: proposals, born proposed, awaiting human promotion.

[turn ? — done] Read the vision, foam/FACTORIO.md §2-4, plant/CLAUDE.md, production.mjs, both existing levels, level-view.js, index.html and all six selftests to find the next non-speculative, non-duplicate piece of vision priority 3 ('a level someone can lose'). LEVEL_1 and LEVEL_2 each expose exactly one knob controlling one fixed bottleneck; the open beads already cover priorities 1 (production, oracle already built), 2 (placement in a real pocket, lp-39d6e7) and gate 7 (lp-484b7f), so I did not touch those. I proposed exactly one new ticket: LEVEL_3, a two-stage production chain (ore -> miner -> smelter -> depot) with two independently player-set processor capacities, so the bottleneck can be either knob rather than a fixed one — a genuinely new mechanic, not a restyled LEVEL_1. It needs zero changes to level-view.js or production.mjs (confirmed via the standing finding that the renderer is already level-agnostic, and by choosing numbers so the source never binds and achieved = min(minerCapacity, smelterCapacity) exactly, staying legible from the capacity numbers already on screen). Kept to one proposal this turn rather than padding with speculative infrastructure work — considered and explicitly rejected exposing production.mjs's per-node achieved amounts, since no shipped level needs it yet and 'perfecting anything in plant/ that no level uses yet' is out of scope.

beads.title: LEVEL_3's numbers are chosen so achieved = min(minerCapacity, smelterCapacity) exactly, with no source-side reduction
beads.body: The ore source rate (300) is set far above anything either processor's slider range can ever consume, exactly LEVEL_1's own device for keeping the source from being the bottleneck. That makes a two-knob level legible from the two capacity numbers drawLevel already prints on each processor's box, with no need to expose production.mjs's per-node throughput or change level-view.js's rendering. Considered proposing that oracle change (it would let a future level highlight the actual bottleneck node instead of only the terminal sink, which is all `deficits` ever names) and deliberately did not: no shipped level needs it yet, and the vision is explicit that perfecting infrastructure nothing consumes is out of scope. Recorded here so a future turn that DOES need it doesn't have to rediscover this reasoning.

beads.title: Filed no asks this turn — decided and built instead
beads.body: Seven asks are already waiting unanswered, several already about level mechanics (lp-02e2be, lp-0f1e21). Rather than add an eighth in the same territory, followed the standing pattern (lp-02e2be's own resolution: 'Built a discrete-choice level as a considered response... instead of waiting on it') and the vision's explicit 'you do not need my sign-off to finish a turn' — proposed LEVEL_3 directly.

beads.title: LEVEL_3: a two-stage production chain where the bottleneck can be either of two player-set capacities
beads.body:
Vision priority 3, 'A LEVEL SOMEONE CAN LOSE': LEVEL_1 (plant/levels/level1.mjs) and LEVEL_2 (plant/levels/level2.mjs) each expose exactly one knob controlling one fixed bottleneck. This is the next level, and it is a genuinely different mechanic already supported by production.mjs and level-view.js with zero renderer changes needed — per the standing finding that 'level-view.js's drawLevel/verdictLine/withSourceRate are already level-agnostic — a second level or a second knob needs no rendering-logic changes'.

Build plant/levels/level3.mjs, exporting LEVEL_3 — a four-node linear chain (satisfies production.mjs's v1 restriction of at most one outgoing edge per node: this is a straight line, no fan-out, no convergence):

  ore (source, rate 300) -> miner (processor, inputs [{resource:'ore',rate:1}], outputs [{resource:'ingot',rate:1}], capacity 70)
  -> smelter (processor, inputs [{resource:'ingot',rate:1}], outputs [{resource:'gear',rate:1}], capacity 45)
  -> depot (sink, resource 'gear', demand 44)

Ore's rate (300) is deliberately far above anything either processor can ever consume (the slider ranges below top out at 100) — LEVEL_1's own device for keeping the source from ever being the bottleneck, reused so the puzzle is only ever about the two processor capacities.

Hand-computed as shipped: scale_miner = min(70, 300/1) = 70 -> ingot flow 70. scale_smelter = min(45, 70/1) = 45 -> gear flow 45. depot achieved = 45 against demand 44 -> margin = (45-44)/44 ≈ 0.02272727, band(margin) === 'tight' — LEVEL_1's own texture: opens feasible, barely.

The new mechanic: TWO independently player-set processor capacities, not one. Because ore never binds, achieved always equals min(minerCapacity, smelterCapacity) exactly — no hidden arithmetic, so the level stays legible from the two capacity numbers drawLevel already prints on each processor's box (line2: `capacity ${n.capacity}`), with no change needed to level-view.js's rendering or to production.mjs's `achieved` map. (Exposing production.mjs's per-node achieved so a bottleneck could be highlighted directly was considered and rejected this turn — no shipped level needs it, and 'perfecting anything in plant/ that no level uses yet' is explicitly out of scope. LEVEL_3's numbers are chosen specifically so this isn't needed.) Whichever slider drags the pair's minimum below 44 starves the depot — dragging EITHER one down breaks it, which is the actual new lesson: the bottleneck is not fixed to one knob the way it is in LEVEL_1 or LEVEL_2.

Build plant/test/level3.selftest.mjs (does not exist yet — this is the gate this ticket brings into being; run as `node plant/test/level3.selftest.mjs`). Match the house style already set by plant/test/level1.selftest.mjs and plant/test/level2.selftest.mjs: every number checked against a hand computation, not truthiness; every positive case paired with a CONTROL; exactly the boundary-bracketing cases per the standing finding that a full slider sweep has zero marginal detection value ('don't sweep a grid — two cases that bracket the boundary beat twenty that don't', lp-dff7a6). Required cases:

1. LEVEL_3 as shipped: feasible, achieved.depot === 45 (within 1e-9), margin within 1e-9 of 45/44 - 1, band(margin) === 'tight', zero deficits.
2. CONTROL A — miner capacity dropped to 40 via level-view.js's existing withProcessorCapacity(LEVEL_3, 'miner', 40), smelter untouched at 45: infeasible, achieved.depot === 40, margin within 1e-9 of -4/44, deficit names depot/gear, and assert the patched network's smelter capacity is still 45 (control-of-control, matching level1.selftest.mjs's own pattern).
3. CONTROL B — smelter capacity dropped to 40 via withProcessorCapacity(LEVEL_3, 'smelter', 40), miner untouched at 70: infeasible, achieved.depot === 40. Assert CONTROL A and CONTROL B produce byte-identical achieved.depot and margin — the proof that either knob alone can be the bottleneck, not just one of them, which is the level's whole point.
4. withProcessorCapacity does not mutate LEVEL_3 (re-stringify check, mirroring level2.selftest.mjs's existing no-mutation pattern).

Wire it into plant/index.html: a third 'Level 3' section following the existing Level 1 / Level 2 pattern (new <h2>, a .stage block with svg#lvl3 + a #lvl3Verdict div, two range inputs for miner/smelter capacity each with a value readout, a reset button), importing LEVEL_3 from ./levels/level3.mjs and reusing feasible/drawLevel/verdictLine/withProcessorCapacity exactly as the Level 2 block already does — call withProcessorCapacity twice, once per processor id, since it is pure and composes cleanly.

Bounded paths (R3): plant/levels/level3.mjs (new), plant/test/level3.selftest.mjs (new), plant/index.html (an additive section plus its script block only — no edits to the existing Level 1 or Level 2 sections). Does not touch plant/level-view.js or plant/production.mjs. Independent (R4) of the other open beads (lp-f25c2f atomic multi-insert, lp-39d6e7 pocket-legality, lp-484b7f frame budget) — none of them touch levels/ or index.html. Reversible (R6): a failed attempt only adds new files and one new section; reverting is deleting them.

[turn 12 — done] Built plant/levels/level3.mjs (LEVEL_3: ore rate 300 -> miner capacity 70 -> smelter capacity 45 -> depot demand 44, exactly the network the ticket specified) and plant/test/level3.selftest.mjs (four cases: shipped-state exactness including band()==='tight', CONTROL A dropping miner capacity to 40, CONTROL B dropping smelter capacity to 40 with an assertion that A and B produce byte-identical achieved.depot and margin, and a no-mutation check on withProcessorCapacity). Wired a third 'Level 3' section into plant/index.html following the existing Level 1/Level 2 pattern exactly: new h2/p, a .stage block with svg#lvl3 + #lvl3Verdict, two range inputs (miner/smelter capacity, 10-100, matching the ticket's stated slider ceiling) with value readouts, a reset button, and a script block importing LEVEL_3 from ./levels/level3.mjs and reusing feasible/drawLevel/verdictLine/withProcessorCapacity already imported for Level 1/2 — composed via withProcessorCapacity(withProcessorCapacity(LEVEL_3,'miner',x),'smelter',y) since the function is pure. No edits to level-view.js, production.mjs, or the existing Level 1/2 sections. All hand-computed numbers were traced by hand against production.mjs's documented feasible() algorithm (scale = min(capacity, supply/inputRate) walked in topological order) since this turn had no Bash to execute the gate — see the recorded finding below, the standing gap on every level/gate ticket so far.

beads.title: This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — the eighth ticket in a row with this exact structural gap
beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is `node plant/test/level3.selftest.mjs`, a shell command. Every number (miner scale min(70,300/1)=70; smelter scale min(45,70/1)=45; depot achieved 45 vs demand 44; margin 45/44-1; CONTROL A/B both collapsing to scale 40 -> achieved 40 -> margin -4/44) was hand-traced through production.mjs's documented feasible() algorithm and cross-checked for the CONTROL A/B byte-identity claim by tracing the exact sequence of Math.min calls each produces (both terminate at the literal integer 40 before any division, so the later margin subtraction (40-44)/44 is bit-identical, not merely close). Confidence is high but this is inference, not execution. Same shape as lp-dfad42, lp-138b76, the production.mjs/level1/band()/level-view/level2 turns: repeating the standing recommendation an eighth time because nothing has changed at the source — either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a shell command, or make explicit in the ticket body that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn.

beads.title: No new CSS added for #lvl3 — reused the untargeted class-only styling Level 2's svg already relies on
beads.body: index.html's <style> block only has ID-specific rules for svg#lvl (width/height/display, and .ln/.ls font+fill under svg#lvl specifically) — svg#lvl2 was never given matching rules when Level 2 shipped, and it is live in production regardless, so those declarations are either non-load-bearing (inherited/default SVG text rendering is adequate) or a pre-existing minor gap outside this ticket's bounded paths (plant/index.html's existing Level 1/Level 2 sections are explicitly off-limits). I mirrored Level 2's approach exactly rather than introduce a new svg#lvl3 rule set, since the ticket scoped this turn to 'an additive section plus its script block only.' Reversible: if a future turn wants the font/fill rules applied uniformly, the fix is a one-line CSS generalization (svg#lvl, svg#lvl2, svg#lvl3 { ... }) done as its own turn, not bundled here.

beads.title: Level 3 never shows which of the two capacities is currently binding — is that ambiguity good friction or bad confusion?
beads.body:
Level 1 and Level 2 each have exactly one thing that can be wrong, so the verdict line alone always explains the failure. Level 3 has two independent capacities and the page deliberately does not highlight which one is currently the tighter constraint (per the ticket's own explicit decision to not expose production.mjs's per-node achieved rates this turn) — a visitor sees 'depot short by N' and has to experiment with both sliders to find out why. That could read as the level's whole point (forcing you to form a hypothesis and test it, which is closer to the vision's playability bar than a single slider ever was) or as it just being confusing on a small phone screen with two sliders and one vague error.

DO: Open plant.minomobi.com, scroll to Level 3, and drag only ONE slider at a time without reading this ask first — see how many drags it takes before you understand which knob you moved actually caused the change.

WATCH FOR: Whether you instinctively drag both sliders at once to 'search' for the answer, versus isolating one variable at a time the way the CONTROL structure in the test does.

SO THAT: If it reads as fine friction, Level 4 (convergence, proposed above) can ship with the same no-highlight approach. If it reads as confusing, the next level turn should add a lightweight per-processor 'binding' indicator (e.g. bold the capacity number that currently equals the achieved output) before building a fourth level with the same blind-spot.

beads.title: LEVEL_4: convergence — two sources feeding one processor's two inputs
beads.body: LEVEL_1/2/3 are all straight lines (production.mjs's v1 forbids fan-out, but CONVERGENCE — several incoming edges feeding one node's inputs, same or different resources — is explicitly allowed and documented in production.mjs's header, and no shipped level has ever exercised it: feasible()'s per-input supply-summing code path (`inc[input.resource] || 0` accumulated across multiple incoming edges before the scale = min(...) computation) is currently untested at the level layer, only at the synthetic-network layer in production.selftest.mjs. Per lp-dff7a6's lesson, this is coverage where the implementation actually branches, not a decorative sweep. Proposed shape: ore (source, rate 200) and coal (source, rate 200) both feed furnace (processor, inputs [{resource:'ore',rate:1},{resource:'coal',rate:1}], outputs [{resource:'steel',rate:1}], capacity 50) -> depot (sink, resource 'steel', demand 48). Hand-computed: scale = min(50, 200/1, 200/1) = 50 -> steel out 50, achieved.depot 50, margin = (50-48)/48 = 1/24 ~= 0.04167, band 'tight'. A CONTROL should drop one source's rate (not both) below what furnace needs, proving BOTH inputs must be supplied, not just capacity. Build plant/levels/level4.mjs, plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs (house style: hand-computed numbers, paired controls, no slider-sweep grid), and an additive Level 4 section in plant/index.html mirroring Level 3's two-slider pattern (one slider per source rate this time, not per processor capacity). Bounded paths: those three files only, no edits to production.mjs, level-view.js, or existing level sections.

beads.title: Planning run 2026-08-05T07:50:31Z
beads.body:
A plan seat was staffed because the ready queue was starved. Output: proposals, born proposed, awaiting human promotion.

[turn ? — done] Gate 5 (production feasibility) is already built and passing on disk per the ledger, and the placement-in-a-real-pocket priority reaches into foam/, which this turn cannot touch and which lp-39d6e7 already owns. So this turn stays on vision priority 3, 'a level someone can lose', and pushes it one mechanic deeper than levels 1-3: all three shipped levels are single-input linear chains, but production.mjs's convergence path (several producers feeding one consumer's DIFFERENT inputs) has only ever been exercised by synthetic fixtures, never by a level, and level-view.js's drawLevel() silently drops any source past the first because it walks from a single node. I propose a fourth level built on convergence, a generalization of drawLevel() to render it (with its own regression proof that the existing three levels render byte-identically), and closing two documented-but-untested gaps in gate 5's own oracle. All three proposals are file-disjoint and none depends on another landing first.

beads.title: Scoped away from placement-in-a-real-pocket and cosmetic UI, toward deeper interaction on what already ships
beads.body: Vision priority 2 (placement in a real foamworld pocket) needs foam/, which the loop cannot touch and which lp-39d6e7 already owns as an open bead — proposing it again would duplicate open work outside this turn's reach. Vision priority 1 (production feasibility) reads 'to build' in FACTORIO.md's table but the ledger already has two findings that the oracle (production.mjs feasible()+band()) is fully built and passing — proposing it again would be rediscovering a finished thing. That leaves priority 3, and the prior turn's own decision to go deeper rather than toward placement-legality or cosmetic UI (three of those were rejected with no reason recorded, per lp-8f8836) — this turn continues that trend rather than re-testing it.

beads.title: LEVEL_4 uses symmetric ore=50/coal=50 so both single-resource controls land on byte-identical achieved/margin
beads.body: Mirrors LEVEL_3's proof shape exactly (CONTROL A and CONTROL B produce byte-identical achieved.depot and margin) but for the orthogonal axis: LEVEL_3 has two SEQUENTIAL capacities, either of which can bottleneck a linear chain — a lesson levels 1 and 2 could not teach. LEVEL_4 has two CONCURRENT resources converging into one recipe, either of which can starve it independently even when the other is abundant and the processor's own capacity is not the constraint — a lesson none of levels 1-3 could teach because none of them has more than one input. Symmetric numbers make the 'either one alone chokes it to the same result' proof mechanical rather than coincidental.

beads.title: drawLevel's convergence generalization must reproduce today's single-chain layout byte-for-byte, not just 'not crash'
beads.body: drawLevel() has zero existing test coverage (level-view.selftest.mjs only covers the two pure functions, withSourceRate and verdictLine) — changing its layout algorithm blind is exactly how a change that scores green quietly breaks the one thing three shipped, played, screenshotted levels depend on. The ticket requires the new gate to pin LEVEL_1's rendered node order and count as an explicit regression check, not just add a new convergence case.

beads.title: LEVEL_4: a foundry that needs two resources at once — production.mjs's convergence path, finally exercised by a level
beads.body:
Levels 1-3 (plant/levels/level1.mjs, level2.mjs, level3.mjs) are all single-input linear chains — every processor in every shipped level has exactly one input resource. production.mjs's header explicitly documents a second capability, CONVERGENCE, that no level has ever used: 'several producers ... may feed one consumer's inputs, same resource or different ... only OUTGOING degree is capped.' plant/test/production.selftest.mjs already has a synthetic convergence fixture (two sources 'a'/'b' feeding a two-input processor 'p') proving feasible() computes it correctly, but that fixture is a code-path exercise, not a level with a narrative a stranger could be handed, the same gap level1.mjs closed for the basic single-chain case (see level1.mjs's own header: 'Everything built against production.mjs so far ... is a synthetic network invented to exercise one code path. This is the other direction.').

Bounded paths: plant/levels/level4.mjs (new), plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs (new). Touch nothing else — this ticket does not wire the level into index.html or touch level-view.js (see the paired proposal below for the rendering half; deliberately independent per R4).

The shape — four nodes, one processor with two inputs:

  ore   (source, resource 'ore', rate 50)
  coal  (source, resource 'coal', rate 50)
  foundry (processor, inputs [{resource:'ore',rate:1},{resource:'coal',rate:1}], outputs [{resource:'steel',rate:1}], capacity 100)
  depot (sink, resource 'steel', demand 48)
  edges: ore->foundry, coal->foundry, foundry->depot

Export as LEVEL_4 = { nodes: [...], edges: [...] } in production.mjs's existing node/edge shape (match level3.mjs's file structure and header-comment style).

Hand-computed numbers for the selftest, mirroring plant/test/level3.selftest.mjs's structure (shipped case + two controls + control-of-control unmutated-input checks), every value checked against a value computed by hand, never just truthiness, per the ledger finding that a self-authored gate certifies absence-of-regression, not presence-of-correctness — so every positive needs a paired CONTROL that must fail:

SHIPPED: scale = min(capacity 100, ore-supply 50/1, coal-supply 50/1) = 50 -> steel out = 50. depot demand 48 -> achieved 50. margin = (50-48)/48 = 1/24 ≈ 0.041667 -> band(margin) === 'tight' (0 <= 0.0417 < 0.15).

CONTROL A — ore dropped to 30 (coal untouched at 50): scale = min(100, 30, 50) = 30 -> achieved 30, short of demand 48 by 18. margin = (30-48)/48 = -0.375. Assert coal's node in the patched copy still reads rate 50 (control of the control, unchanged).

CONTROL B — coal dropped to 30 (ore untouched at 50): scale = min(100, 50, 30) = 30 -> achieved 30, margin = -0.375. Assert ore's node in this patched copy still reads rate 50. Assert CONTROL A and CONTROL B produce byte-identical achieved.depot and byte-identical margin (rA.achieved.depot === rB.achieved.depot, rA.margin === rB.margin) — the whole point, mirroring level3.selftest.mjs's own cross-check: either resource alone bottlenecks the recipe to the exact same result, which is the lesson no existing level teaches.

Build the two control networks by mapping over LEVEL_4.nodes and overriding the named source's rate (LEVEL_4 has two sources, so level-view.js's existing withSourceRate helper — which overrides ALL sources at once — is not usable here; write the override inline in the test file, the same way level3.selftest.mjs constructs its variants). Also assert LEVEL_4 itself is unchanged after both control constructions (re-stringify matches a pre-call snapshot), matching level3.selftest.mjs's own no-mutation check.

No slider sweep across the full range — per the ledger finding on lp-dff7a6, a coverage matrix whose axes the implementation does not branch on has zero marginal detection value. Exactly the boundary-bracketing cases above, same as level3.selftest.mjs.

beads.title: level-view.js: generalize drawLevel() to render convergence (two sources into one processor) — it currently drops any source past the first
beads.body:
plant/level-view.js's drawLevel() walks a single chain: `let cur = level.nodes.find(n => n.kind === 'source')` picks the FIRST source only, then follows `next.get(cur.id)` (built from `Map(level.edges.map(e => [e.from, e.to]))`) until it runs out. For any network with more than one source converging into a processor — exactly the shape production.mjs already supports and the paired LEVEL_4 proposal above would add — this silently renders 3 boxes instead of 4: it does not throw, it just drops the second source and everyone downstream still looks correct. That is a confident lie, the same failure mode plant/test/view.selftest.mjs's own header warns about for the summon inspector.

Bounded paths: plant/level-view.js, plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs. Independent of the LEVEL_4 proposal above — this ticket must build its own inline convergence fixture for the regression test rather than importing plant/levels/level4.mjs, so neither proposal orders the other (R4). Reuse the exact 'a'/'b'/'p'/'s' convergence network already inline in plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs's verdictLine tests (two sources, one two-input processor, one sink) as that fixture — it is already in the file, already hand-verified elsewhere (plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's own convergence case), and needs no new arithmetic.

The fix: replace the single-source walk with a layered column assignment. Build `incoming` (id -> [predecessor ids]) from `level.edges`. Each node's column = 0 if it has no incoming edges (a source), else 1 + the max column of its predecessors (memoized recursion — the network is guaranteed acyclic, production.mjs refuses cycles outright). Group nodes by column; nodes sharing a column stack vertically, evenly spaced across the SVG's height, in `level.nodes` order (matches the file's existing determinism convention — order comes from the literal, not object iteration). Draw exactly one outgoing arrow per node via the existing `next.get(id)` (still safe — production.mjs's v1 restriction caps every node at ONE outgoing edge; only the incoming side ever fans out, which is what this generalizes for). For a single-chain level every column holds exactly one node, so the fix must reduce to today's box positions and left-to-right order exactly.

drawLevel()'s only interaction with its `svg` argument is `svg.innerHTML = parts.join('\n')` — it never reads from it — so the selftest needs no real DOM, just a plain object `{ innerHTML: '' }` passed where index.html would pass a real SVG element.

Gate assertions to add to plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs:
1. Backward-compat regression: call drawLevel on a stub svg with LEVEL_1 (already imported in this file) and the corresponding feasible() verdict; assert the ids 'ore', 'smelter', 'depot' each appear exactly once in svg.innerHTML, and that their first-appearance indices are strictly increasing (ore before smelter before depot) — proving the linear layout is unchanged.
2. Convergence, the actual bug: call drawLevel on a stub svg with the a/b/p/s fixture and its feasible() verdict; assert svg.innerHTML contains BOTH 'a' and 'b' (today it contains only whichever `Array.prototype.find` returns first) and that the rendered box count (occurrences of '<rect') equals 4, matching the fixture's node count — today it renders 3.
3. No throw: drawLevel must not throw for the convergence fixture (today it does not throw either — it silently drops a node, which is the more dangerous failure, so this assertion documents the current safe-but-wrong behavior is now fixed, not just non-crashing).

[turn 13 — done] Replaced drawLevel()'s single-source chain walk with a layered column layout: each node's column is 0 if it has no incoming edges, else 1 + the max column of its predecessors (memoized recursion over an `incoming` map built from level.edges), nodes sharing a column stack vertically with even spacing across the SVG height in level.nodes order, and each node still draws at most one outgoing arrow via the existing `next` map (safe because production.mjs v1 caps outgoing degree at 1 — only the incoming side ever fans in). Verified by hand that for any single-chain level every column holds exactly one node and the formulas (x per column, y = (ri+1)*rowGap-bh/2 with rowGap=H/(col.length+1)) reduce byte-for-byte to the old positions when col.length===1, so LEVEL_1 renders identically. Added two new gate blocks to plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs: a regression check that LEVEL_1 still renders ore/smelter/depot exactly once each, left-to-right; and a convergence check using an inline a/b/p/s two-source fixture (identical to the one already hand-verified elsewhere in this same test file) asserting both sources render, the box count is 4, and drawLevel does not throw. Did not run the gate — this turn had no Bash — so this is inference from tracing the code and the arithmetic by hand, not execution; same structural gap noted on every prior ticket in this chain.

beads.title: production.mjs: close two documented-but-untested gaps in gate 5's own oracle — zero-sink vacuity and multi-sink margin-is-the-minimum
beads.body:
production.mjs's feasible() JSDoc names two behaviors that plant/test/production.selftest.mjs never exercises, both flagged in the source as gaps: (1) 'A network with no sinks is vacuously feasible and reports margin 0 ... not exercised by any ticket case, recorded as a decision rather than left to fall out silently' (production.mjs's own comment, lines ~144-145); (2) 'margin — min over sinks of (achieved - demand)/demand' implies more than one sink can exist in a network, but every fixture across production.selftest.mjs, level-view.selftest.mjs and all three shipped levels has EXACTLY one sink — the min-across-sinks logic (`margin = Math.min(margin, ...)` inside the loop in feasible()) has never been exercised by more than one term.

Bounded paths: plant/test/production.selftest.mjs only — no changes to production.mjs itself; this is closing a coverage gap in an already-correct, already-shipped oracle, not changing its behavior. This is gate-5 measurement rigor in the vision's own terms: 'plan the measurement, not just the work' — the gate itself is the thing being strengthened here.

Two new cases, in the file's existing style (every value checked against a hand computation, never just truthiness; every positive paired with a CONTROL where useful):

1. Zero-sink network: `{ nodes: [{ kind: 'source', id: 'src', resource: 'iron', rate: 5 }], edges: [] }` (a lone source, nothing downstream — legal per analyse(), since sinks are not required to exist). Assert feasible() returns `{ ok: true, deficits: [], margin: 0 }` exactly — `ok` is `true` (deficits.length === 0 vacuously), `deficits` is an empty array, and `margin` is exactly `0` (not `Infinity`, which is what the loop variable is seeded with before the 'no sinks at all' fallback in feasible()'s source fires). CONTROL: the same network but with one sink added and starved (e.g. add `{ kind: 'sink', id: 'snk', resource: 'iron', demand: 100 }` and the edge `{ from: 'src', to: 'snk' }`) must NOT report margin 0 or ok true — proving the zero-sink case is a real code path, not a coincidental default that also happens to fire when a sink exists.

2. Multi-sink network: one source feeding two sinks would need fan-out from the source, which production.mjs refuses (v1 restriction, already covered by the fan-out test) — so build it as two independent chains sharing no nodes, e.g. `src1 -> snk1` (rate 10, demand 4, margin computed by hand) and `src2 -> snk2` (rate 3, demand 4, margin computed by hand, negative) as ONE network literal (two disconnected components are legal — analyse()'s topological sort does not require connectivity). Hand-compute both margins, assert `feasible(net).margin` equals `Math.min(marginOfSnk1, marginOfSnk2)` exactly, and assert `deficits` contains exactly the starved sink (snk2) and not the satisfied one (snk1) — proving the reported margin is genuinely the minimum across sinks and not, say, the last sink evaluated in topological order (which for this fixture would give the wrong answer if the two chains were ordered the other way, since JS object/array order here is insertion order from `nodes`, not sink-declaration order).

beads.title: Arrows between differing rows draw as a straight diagonal, not the old horizontal-only path
beads.body: The old arrow path always connected two boxes at the same H/2 y-coordinate, so its arrowhead triangle (`l-6 -4 v8 z`) was drawn assuming a horizontal line. The new layout can connect boxes in different rows (e.g. a converging source above/below its sibling), so the line from box-right-mid to box-left-mid is diagonal while the arrowhead triangle is still drawn axis-aligned to the target's left edge rather than rotated to the line's actual angle. This is a cosmetic simplification, not a correctness issue — the gate only checks box/id presence and count, not arrow geometry — and it was chosen over computing a rotated arrowhead because no ticket or test asked for one and the vision explicitly prioritizes 'ugly and playable' over polish on plant/. Reversal condition: if a future ticket wants visually correct arrow angles for multi-row levels, rotate the arrowhead by atan2(by-ay, bx-ax).

beads.title: This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — the ninth ticket in a row with this exact structural gap
beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is `node plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs`, a shell command. The layout math was hand-traced to prove exact reduction to the pre-existing single-chain positions for LEVEL_1 (gap, x, y, and arrow endpoint formulas all collapse to the old values when every column holds one node), and the convergence fixture's column assignment was hand-traced (a,b at column 0; p at column 1; s at column 2). Confidence is high but this is inference, not execution. Same shape as lp-dfad42, lp-138b76, and six subsequent tickets (production.mjs, level1, band(), level-view withSourceRate/verdictLine, level2, level3) — repeating the standing recommendation a ninth time because nothing has changed at the source: either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a shell command, or make explicit in the ticket body that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn.

beads.title: Scoped this turn toward oracle behaviours no level exercises yet (convergence, multi-sink), not toward placement-in-a-pocket or frame-budget
