beads.title: LEVEL_5 (multi-sink) deliberately does not wire into index.html this turn
beads.body: LEVEL_4 needs a new withSourceRateById in level-view.js and touches index.html; if LEVEL_5 also touched index.html the two proposals would share a file and violate R4 (independent, no hidden ordering against a sibling). LEVEL_5 needs zero changes to production.mjs or level-view.js (Kahn's algorithm and drawLevel's column layout already handle disconnected components), so its whole ticket is level file + gate file only, and wiring it into the page is left for a follow-up once a human has looked at whether 'two goals, only the worse one counts' is worth surfacing — the same call already made and recorded for LEVEL_4's own wiring in an earlier turn.

beads.title: LEVEL_4 — a convergence level: two sources feed one processor, either can starve it
beads.body:
Build LEVEL_4, a convergence-shaped level: two independently-metered sources (ore, coal) feed one processor (furnace) that emits ingot into a single sink (depot). This is a new lesson none of LEVEL_1/2/3 teaches: today's oracle already handles convergence (production.mjs's header: 'CONVERGENCE stays allowed... several producers may feed one consumer's inputs') and level-view.js's drawLevel already renders it correctly (plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs's 'drawLevel: convergence' case, which pins that two sources into one processor must not drop either) — but no LEVEL_N file has ever put a player in front of it. Right now convergence is only exercised by synthetic fixtures invented to test code paths, exactly the gap the vision's measurement-backlog framing is about: production.mjs's own machinery is ahead of what any level asks a stranger to actually do.

Shape (bounded to plant/levels/level4.mjs, new file):
  ore  (source, rate 50)   -\
                             +-> furnace (inputs ore:1, coal:1 -> output ingot:1, capacity 55) -> depot (sink, demand 48)
  coal (source, rate 50)   -/

Hand-computed: scale = min(capacity 55, ore-supply 50/1, coal-supply 50/1) = 50 (supply-bound on BOTH inputs at once, capacity never binds) -> achieved 50, margin = (50-48)/48 = 1/24 ≈ 0.0417 -> band(margin) is 'tight' (matches LEVEL_1's and LEVEL_3's own texture: opens feasible, barely). Because ore and coal ship at the SAME rate (50/50), the level is symmetric by construction: dropping either resource alone to the same value X<50 produces byte-identical achieved/depot and margin — the exact kind of paired CONTROL/CONTROL-of-CONTROL structure level3.selftest.mjs already uses for its two-capacity level, applied here to two-SOURCE convergence instead of two-processor chaining.

level-view.js currently has no way to move ONE named source independently — withSourceRate (plant/level-view.js) overrides every source node's rate at once, which is correct for LEVEL_1 (exactly one source) but wrong for LEVEL_4 (two). Add:
  export function withSourceRateById(level, sourceId, rate) {
    return { ...level, nodes: level.nodes.map((n) => (n.id === sourceId && n.kind === 'source' ? { ...n, rate } : n)) };
  }
and extend plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs with known-answer cases for it (mirrors the existing withSourceRate cases: overrides only the named source, leaves every other node byte-identical, does not mutate the input).

Wire into plant/index.html as a fourth stage ('Level 4 — two ingredients, either can run out'): two range sliders (ore, coal, e.g. min 10 max 70), each calling withSourceRateById(LEVEL_4, 'ore'|'coal', value) then feasible()+drawLevel()+verdictLine(), reset button restoring both to 50 — same pattern LEVEL_1/2/3's <script> blocks already use, no new rendering code needed since drawLevel's layered-column layout already handles multiple same-column source nodes (verified by the existing convergence case in level-view.selftest.mjs).

Gate: plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs (new — creates-gate) checks: shipped level is feasible with achieved.depot===50 and margin matching 1/24 by hand; CONTROL A (ore dropped to 40, coal untouched) is infeasible with achieved.depot===40; CONTROL B (coal dropped to 40, ore untouched) produces byte-identical achieved/margin to CONTROL A (the symmetry the shipped numbers were chosen to prove); a CONTROL-of-the-CONTROL confirms the untouched source/capacity numbers didn't move; and withSourceRateById does not mutate its input. Also update plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs with withSourceRateById's own known-answer cases. Both must pass, and the whole existing suite must still pass.

R3 bounded paths: plant/levels/level4.mjs (new), plant/level-view.js, plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs (new), plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs, plant/index.html — all under plant/.
R4 independent of the LEVEL_5 proposal below: disjoint files, no shared edit target.
R5 memory: production.mjs's own header ('CONVERGENCE stays allowed...'), level-view.selftest.mjs's existing convergence-rendering case, level3.selftest.mjs's CONTROL/CONTROL-of-CONTROL pattern (reused here), and the standing finding that a self-authored gate 'certifies no regression, not the new behaviour' — hence the explicit byte-identical-achieved symmetry check, not just truthiness.
R6 reversible: purely additive (one new level file, one new gate file, one new exported function plus its own tests, one new index.html section) — a bad attempt reverts cleanly.

beads.title: LEVEL_5 — two independent sinks: the worse of two goals governs, not the only one
beads.body:
Build LEVEL_5: two fully independent one-line chains (oreA->smelterA->depotA, oreB->smelterB->depotB) sharing no node or edge, so the level has TWO sinks instead of one. This exercises a part of production.mjs's own oracle that has never been driven by any level or even any test fixture with more than one sink: feasible()'s margin is documented as 'min over sinks of (achieved-demand)/demand' and its deficits array is built to hold one entry per failing sink, but every existing fixture (production.selftest.mjs, level1/2/3.selftest.mjs) has exactly one sink, so 'more than one deficit' and 'the minimum sink governs the margin, not the only sink' have zero coverage anywhere in the repo. This is the gap the vision's 'plan the measurement, not just the work' section is about: the code the oracle needs for this already exists (feasible()'s per-sink loop, unchanged), only the level and the gate that would exercise it do not.

Shape (bounded to plant/levels/level5.mjs, new file — production.mjs and level-view.js are untouched, both already handle disconnected components: Kahn's algorithm seeds its queue from every node with in-degree 0, which both oreA and oreB satisfy independently):

  oreA (source, rate 60) -> smelterA (in ore:1 -> out gearA:1, capacity 40) -> depotA (sink, resource gearA, demand 38)
  oreB (source, rate 30) -> smelterB (in ore:1 -> out gearB:1, capacity 50) -> depotB (sink, resource gearB, demand 28)

Hand-computed, as shipped:
  chain A: scale = min(40, 60/1) = 40 -> achieved.depotA = 40, margin_A = (40-38)/38 = 1/19 ≈ 0.0526
  chain B: scale = min(50, 30/1) = 30 -> achieved.depotB = 30, margin_B = (30-28)/28 = 1/14 ≈ 0.0714
  overall: ok = true (both sinks cleared), margin = min(margin_A, margin_B) = margin_A ≈ 0.0526 (chain A governs even though chain B is untouched and fine) -> band 'tight'.

CONTROL A — starve only chain A (oreA rate 60->20): scale_A = min(40,20)=20 -> achieved.depotA=20 < 38, ONE deficit (depotA only); chain B is completely untouched and still clears (achieved.depotB=30>=28) — proving a level can fail even though one of its two goals is still fine, which is the new lesson this level exists to teach and no LEVEL_1/2/3 can, since none of them has a second goal to leave alone.

CONTROL B — starve BOTH chains (oreA->20, oreB->10): scale_B = min(50,10)=10 -> achieved.depotB=10<28. Now deficits.length === 2, one per sink — the first case anywhere in this repo where feasible() is asked to report more than one simultaneous shortfall. margin = min(margin_A', margin_B') where both are negative.

No wiring into plant/index.html in this ticket — deliberately, to keep this proposal's file set disjoint from the LEVEL_4 proposal above (R4) and because production.mjs and level-view.js need zero changes to support this (unlike LEVEL_4, which needs a new withSourceRateById), so this is strictly smaller: level file + gate file only. Wiring it into the page is a natural follow-up once a human has looked at whether 'two goals, only the worse one counts' is a texture worth surfacing to a visitor — deferring UI is the same call already made and recorded for LEVEL_4's own wiring in an earlier turn.

Gate: plant/test/level5.selftest.mjs (new — creates-gate): shipped level is feasible, both per-sink achieved values and the overall margin match the hand calc above (margin equals chain A's, not chain B's, proving the min-over-sinks rule is exercised, not just a single-sink pass-through); CONTROL A produces exactly one deficit naming depotA and leaves depotB's achieved value unchanged from the shipped run; CONTROL B produces exactly two deficits; a no-mutation check confirms LEVEL_5 itself is untouched by either control (JSON round-trip pattern already used in level1/level3.selftest.mjs).

R3 bounded paths: plant/levels/level5.mjs (new), plant/test/level5.selftest.mjs (new) — both under plant/, nothing else touched.
R4 independent of the LEVEL_4 proposal above: disjoint files entirely.
R5 memory: production.mjs's own docstring for feasible() ('margin — min over sinks...'), the standing finding that a self-authored gate 'certifies no regression, not the new behaviour' (hence checking the exact per-sink numbers and the deficit COUNT, not just ok/not-ok), and lp-dff7a6's finding that a coverage sweep with no marginal detection value is a wasted turn — this proposal is scoped narrowly to the ONE new axis (sink count) the current suite has never varied.
R6 reversible: two new files only, nothing existing modified.

beads.title: Planning run 2026-08-05T08:12:30Z
beads.body:
A plan seat was staffed because the ready queue was starved. Output: proposals, born proposed, awaiting human promotion.

[turn ? — done] Read the vision, FACTORIO.md, and the graph's proposed backlog before writing anything: gate 5 (production.mjs) is already built and tested, and the two ready foam-tagged beads (lp-f25c2f, lp-39d6e7, lp-484b7f) are not actually dispatchable to a plant/-scoped loop since they require touching foam/, which matches the existing FINDING that the 'ready' queue's foam-tagged items are class-b in practice — the starvation is total, not partial. The proposed backlog already has three near-duplicate LEVEL_4 (convergence) tickets and two LEVEL_5 (multi-sink) tickets sitting unpromoted, plus an already-asked question about why placement-legality/cosmetic-UI proposals keep getting rejected (lp-8f8836) and an already-proposed gap-closing ticket for production.mjs's zero-sink/multi-sink margin behaviour — so I did not re-propose any of that ground. Instead I found a genuinely untouched mechanic: production.mjs has TWO refusal paths (a margin shortfall, and analyse() THROWING on an illegal edge — resource mismatch or fan-out) and every shipped level (1/2/3) only ever exercises the first. The throw path is a harder, more legible 'you formed an intention and got refused for it' than a slider easing toward red, which is exactly the vision's stated bar, so I proposed LEVEL_6 to build it and a small independent hardening ticket to pin the refusal message wording LEVEL_6 will depend on.

beads.title: LEVEL_4 has three near-duplicate proposed tickets and LEVEL_5 has two, none promoted across several planning turns
beads.body: graph.json titles: 'LEVEL_4: convergence — two sources feeding one processor's two inputs', 'LEVEL_4: a foundry that needs two resources at once...', 'LEVEL_4 — a convergence level: two sources feed one processor, either can starve it' (all status proposed), plus 'LEVEL_5 (multi-sink)...' and 'LEVEL_5 — two independent sinks...' (both proposed). Same underlying idea re-proposed by successive turns instead of one being promoted or the rest dropped. This looks like backlog hygiene, not scheduling starvation — a human pass to promote one and drop the rest would free real capacity. I did not add a fourth.

beads.title: Scoped this turn's two proposals away from LEVEL_4/LEVEL_5 and away from placement-legality/cosmetic UI
beads.body: LEVEL_4/LEVEL_5 are already well-covered (see the finding above); placement-legality and cosmetic-UI work already has an open, unanswered ask (lp-8f8836) about why prior attempts were rejected with no reason recorded — proposing more of that ground before the ask resolves would risk the same silent rejection. Went instead for production.mjs's throw-based refusal path, which no level, no test-with-message-assertions, and no other proposed bead currently touches.

beads.title: LEVEL_6's numbers: ore rate 60, smelter capacity 50, depot demand 40 — margin 0.25, comfortable, on purpose
beads.body: The point of this level is the CHOICE (which wiring), not the margin arithmetic — LEVEL_1/2/3 already cover tight-margin tension. A comfortable margin on the 'ok' branch keeps the two illegal branches (resource mismatch, fan-out) the only source of difficulty, so a visitor isn't solving two problems in one screen.

beads.title: LEVEL_6 — a wiring choice where the oracle itself refuses the connection, not just a low margin
beads.body:
Vision's bar for playable: 'an intention they formed, acted on, and got refused for.' LEVEL_1 (slider), LEVEL_2 (capacity-choice button), LEVEL_3 (two capacity sliders) all fail the same way: feasible() runs to completion and reports a margin shortfall. None of them exercise production.mjs's OTHER refusal path — analyse() THROWING when an edge has no shared resource or a node gets a second outgoing edge (plant/production.mjs:87-99, comment block at :9-25 names this the deliberate v1 scope). A thrown refusal is a harder, more legible failure than a red number: the connection itself is illegal, not just tight. Nothing in plant/ renders that state today — index.html and level-view.js only ever call feasible() on networks guaranteed to parse.

Build plant/levels/level6.mjs exporting three full node/edge literals sharing one ore source (rate 60) and one depot (demand 40): 'ok' (ore -> smelter[cap 50] -> depot: scale=min(50,60/1)=50, achieved 50, margin (50-40)/40=0.25, feasible), 'mismatch' (ore -> woodMill[inputs wood/1, outputs plank/1, cap 50] -> depot: emits(ore)=['ore'], accepts(woodMill)=['wood'], no shared resource, analyse() throws containing 'no shared resource'), 'fanout' (ore feeds BOTH smelter and a second sink 'stockpile'[resource ore, demand 5]: two outgoing edges from 'ore', analyse() throws containing 'fan-out'). Each is a complete network, not a parameter patch — the player picks a WIRING, not a number.

Add to plant/level-view.js: `safeFeasible(network)` that calls feasible() and, on throw, returns `{ ok:false, refused:true, reason: err.message, achieved:{}, deficits:[] }` instead of propagating; and `refusalLine(v)` (or a branch inside verdictLine keyed on `v.refused`) producing a sentence naming the reason, worded distinctly from a margin failure (e.g. '✗ refused: <reason>' vs verdictLine's existing '✗ <sink> wanted...'). Wire a Level 6 section into plant/index.html: three buttons swapping the whole displayed network (mirrors LEVEL_2's SMELTER_OPTIONS.map() button pattern at index.html:296-301, but here the button swaps `level.edges`/`level.nodes` wholesale, not one field), rendered via the existing drawLevel() plus the new refusal-aware verdict line.

Gate (creates it): plant/test/level6.selftest.mjs — for each of the three variants, pins safeFeasible()'s result shape (ok/refused/reason substring for 'mismatch' and 'fanout'; ok:true/refused:false and the hand-computed margin 0.25 for 'ok'); a CONTROL proving feasible() called DIRECTLY (not through safeFeasible) on 'mismatch' and 'fanout' still throws, so safeFeasible is demonstrably catching something real rather than silently no-op'ing on an already-valid network (same paired-CONTROL discipline production.selftest.mjs already uses throughout); and that drawLevel() does not throw when handed a refused verdict shape (achieved:{}, deficits:[]).

Bounded paths: plant/levels/level6.mjs (new), plant/level-view.js, plant/index.html, plant/test/level6.selftest.mjs (new). Reversible: pure additions — verdictLine's existing behaviour for the v.ok/v.deficits shape every current caller uses is unchanged; refusal handling is a new branch keyed on a field (`v.refused`) no existing caller ever sets. Independent (R4) of the LEVEL_4/LEVEL_5 tickets already in the backlog — touches none of their files and needs none of production.mjs's convergence/multi-sink paths.

beads.title: Pin production.mjs's refusal MESSAGES, not just that they throw
beads.body:
plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's `throws(fn)` helper (line 23) only reports true/false — every check in the 'fan-out and cycles' (:101-131), 'resource matching' (:133-152) and 'other refusals' (:154-191) sections confirms feasible() threw and never checks what it said. FACTORIO.md's whole pitch for gate 5 is 'no model opinion anywhere in this file' — the exact wording of a refusal becomes part of that contract the moment anything downstream pattern-matches on `err.message`, which the LEVEL_6 proposal in this same batch does. Today nothing would catch that wording drifting under a future edit to production.mjs.

Add assertions to the EXISTING suite (no new file) checking each refusal's caught message contains its documented cause, reusing the literal strings already at production.mjs's own throw sites: fan-out -> 'fan-out' (:92), cycle -> 'cycle' (:121), no shared resource -> 'no shared resource' (:97), ambiguous resource -> 'ambiguous' (:97), unknown node kind -> 'unknown node kind' (:61), duplicate id -> 'duplicate id' (:63), unknown edge endpoint -> 'unknown node' (:88-89), non-positive rate/demand/capacity -> 'must be positive' (:47), zero inputs -> 'zero inputs' (:71), zero outputs -> 'zero outputs' (:74). Each existing `ok('...', throws(() => feasible(...)))` call in those three sections gets a paired assertion that catches the same call and checks `.message.includes(...)` — reusing the same fixture literal already in the file, so this adds no new networks and no new arithmetic to get wrong (matches the file's own stated house style at :9-12: every case is hand-checked, not just truthy).

Bounded paths: plant/test/production.selftest.mjs only — production.mjs itself is untouched, so this cannot change gate 5's behaviour, only what proves it. Gate: node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs (already exists and passes today; must keep passing with the added assertions, which is the whole point). Independent (R4) of the LEVEL_6 proposal above — either can land without the other; LEVEL_6 pins its own three messages on its own fixtures regardless of whether this ticket lands first.

[turn 14 — done] Added a paired message-content assertion after every existing throw-only assertion in the 'fan-out and cycles', 'resource matching' and 'other refusals' sections of plant/test/production.selftest.mjs, plus a messageOf() helper next to the existing throws() helper. Each new assertion catches the same call already used for the throws() check and asserts .message.includes(<literal cause string>), reusing the exact literal substrings production.mjs's own throw sites use (fan-out, cycle, no shared resource, ambiguous, unknown node kind, duplicate id, unknown node (used for both unknown 'to' and unknown 'from', since production.mjs emits the identical phrase for both), must be positive (used for source rate, sink demand, and processor capacity, since production.mjs's positive() helper emits one shared phrase for all three), zero inputs, zero outputs. No new fixtures, no new networks, no changes to production.mjs itself — only the test file changed. In the 'other refusals' section, each previously-inline feasible({...}) fixture was lifted into a named const so the same network object could be reused for both the throws() check and the messageOf() check without duplicating the literal object; this is a mechanical refactor with no change to any existing fixture's shape or values. I do not have Bash in this turn's tool grant so I could not execute the suite; every substring match was hand-verified character-for-character against production.mjs's own throw-site strings (read in full before writing any assertion), which is the same verification method every prior turn on this file has had to use for the same structural reason.

beads.title: The loop exhausted what a straight line can teach — and the ceiling is fan-out, which is the genre's central decision the oracle refuses
beads.body:
Two hours into the five-hour run: 52 commits, 13 turns, 1 gate failure (turn 9, before the run). Turns 10-13 all passed. And the shape of what it built is the finding.

  turn 10  a selftest for level-view.js — code the OPERATOR shipped untested
  turn 11  level 2 — a discrete three-way machine choice
  turn 12  level 3 — two independent bottlenecks
  turn 13  (level 4 was queued next)

MY FIRST READ WAS WRONG AND IS WORTH RECORDING AS SUCH. Seeing level2, level3 I called it drift — the explainer attractor recurring one level up. Then I read them. Level 1 is one continuous knob, level 2 one discrete choice, level 3 two independently starving bottlenecks. Each teaches something the previous one cannot. That is a difficulty curve, deliberately built, and calling it repetition was a pattern-match on the file names rather than a reading of the contents. I have made the reverse error today too (assuming a planner was cleverly stuck when a length check had eaten its output). The lesson is the same both ways: read the artefact before naming the pattern.

THE REAL CONSTRAINT IS STRUCTURAL AND IT IS INTERESTING. Every level is a straight line, and not by choice: production.mjs v1 THROWS on fan-out. Its own header says why — "with fan-out allowed, how much of a source's output goes to which consumer is itself a variable to solve for", which is a general LP rather than one forward pass.

So the loop is not lazily tiling. It is exhausting what a line topology can express, and it is nearly done: after "two independent bottlenecks" a fourth line-shaped level really is just different numbers.

AND FAN-OUT IS NOT A LIMITATION TO WORK AROUND — IT IS THE GENRE. Splitting a shared output between competing consumers is the central decision a factory game is made of. The oracle currently refuses precisely the thing the game is about. That refusal was correct for v1 (small and exact beats general and slow, and refusing a case honestly beats approximating it silently), and it is now the ceiling.

The same argument that justified gate 5 applies one level up, which is what makes it convincing rather than a preference: until fan-out is decidable, every ticket about CHOOSING WHERE OUTPUT GOES is ungradeable, and ungradeable work is work this system cannot take. Gate 5 bought three levels in two hours by making sources-and-sinks gradeable. Fan-out buys the actual puzzle.

Steered in vision.md rather than by adding a ticket: levels are closed as done, fan-out is priority 1, pocket placement stays priority 2. The planner reads it verbatim on its next turn, which is the mechanism working as designed — a loop pointed at a local optimum is steered by changing what it is pointed at, not by rejecting its output one ticket at a time.

beads.title: Reused the single 'unknown node' and 'must be positive' phrases across multiple distinct causes rather than inventing distinguishing text
beads.body: production.mjs emits the exact same message text for an unknown 'to' node and an unknown 'from' node (both 'production: edge names unknown node "..."'), and the exact same text for a non-positive source rate, sink demand, and processor capacity (all via the shared positive() helper: 'production: ${what} must be positive', where only the interpolated ${what} differs). The ticket's own mapping table already groups these under one cause string each. So the new assertions check the shared substring ('unknown node', 'must be positive') rather than trying to further distinguish 'from' vs 'to' or rate vs demand vs capacity, since production.mjs's own wording does not distinguish them either — asserting a finer distinction than the source code draws would be a test claiming a contract the implementation doesn't have. This would reverse if a future edit to production.mjs's error strings actually differentiated these cases; the existing distinct `ok('an edge naming an unknown "to" node throws', ...)` / `unknown "from"` test names already document which fixture is which, so the finer distinction lives in the test names, not in the message content.

beads.title: This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — the tenth ticket in a row with this exact structural gap
beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is `node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs`, a shell command. Every new assertion is a direct substring check against a literal string copied verbatim from production.mjs's own throw sites (read in full immediately before writing this ticket's changes), which is about as low-risk as this pattern gets since there is no arithmetic or derived value involved anywhere in this change — but it is still inference, not execution. This is now the tenth class-a/creates-gate ticket in the ledger with this identical gap (lp-dfad42, lp-138b76, production.mjs, level1, band(), level-view withSourceRate/verdictLine, level2, level3, level-view layout, and now this one). Repeating the standing recommendation a tenth time because nothing has changed at the source: either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a shell command, or make explicit in the ticket body that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn.

beads.title: Planning run 2026-08-05T08:25:26Z
beads.body:
A plan seat was staffed because the ready queue was starved. Output: proposals, born proposed, awaiting human promotion.

[turn ? — done] Vision names fan-out as the ceiling and 'the real puzzle' — production.mjs v1 refuses any node with more than one outgoing edge, and every level so far is a straight line by force because of it. I read production.mjs, its selftest, and level-view.js to find the exact restriction and its blast radius, then wrote one ticket that lifts it: let an edge carry an explicit numeric share so a node's output can be split across competing consumers, computed correctly by feasible(), with a new gate file that pins the split arithmetic and a paired regression check that the existing no-share fan-out refusal (plant/test/production.selftest.mjs) still throws. I deliberately scoped this to 'the network specifies the split' rather than 'the oracle solves for the optimal split' — the latter is a real LP search and is future work; this ticket builds the layer under it. I chose one focused ticket over several thinner ones, matching the vision's singular priority and the precedent of turn 7's gate-5 build, which also landed a full oracle-plus-gate in one turn.

beads.title: Fan-out ticket scoped to explicit-share (network supplies the split), not solve-for-the-split
beads.body: The vision's own phrasing — 'how much of a source's output goes to which consumer is itself a variable to solve for' — describes a real LP search, which is more than one turn. This ticket builds the prerequisite instead: let a network literal specify a split via an edge's `share` field and make feasible() compute correctly against it. An optimizer that searches over shares is a distinct, later ticket once this lands.

beads.title: Share validation groups by RESOLVED resource, not by node
beads.body: A processor with two different outputs routed to two different single consumers is not competition — it is two independent groups of size 1, and neither edge should be forced to carry a share field. Only edges that resolve to the SAME shared resource on the SAME node are a true fan-out group and require explicit shares summing to <=1. This keeps today's 'each output routed once, no share required' pattern working unchanged.

beads.title: level-view.js's drawLevel() was deliberately left untouched by this proposal
beads.body: drawLevel builds `next = Map(level.edges.map(e => [e.from, e.to]))` (level-view.js:49) — keyed by `from`, so a second outgoing edge from the same node silently overwrites the first and only one arrow ever draws. This is dormant today because production.mjs still refuses multi-edge nodes outright, and stays dormant even after this ticket lands (no level uses fan-out yet, and the vision says stop polishing the explainer/UI). Flagging now so whichever future ticket wires a fan-out level into the page knows to fix `next` into a multi-edge structure first, rather than rediscovering a silently-dropped arrow.

beads.title: Fan-out: explicit per-edge output shares in production.mjs
beads.body:
production.mjs v1 refuses any node with more than one outgoing edge, and its own header says why: 'with fan-out allowed, how much of a source's output goes to which consumer is itself a variable to solve for' (production.mjs:11-15). The vision calls this the ceiling and 'the real puzzle' — splitting a shared output between competing consumers is the genre's central decision, and every level so far is a straight line 'by force, not by choice' (FINDING: 'The loop exhausted what a straight line can teach — and the ceiling is fan-out, which is the genre's central decision the oracle refuses').

This ticket does NOT build the full optimization (solving for the split that maximizes feasibility) — that is a real LP search and stays out of scope for one turn. It builds the layer underneath it: let a network SPECIFY a split and let feasible() compute correctly against it, which is the prerequisite an optimizer would need to search over.

Scope — plant/production.mjs only:

1. An edge MAY carry a numeric `share` field, e.g. `{ from, to, share: 0.6 }`.
2. Resolve each node's outgoing edges into groups by the RESOLVED shared resource (the same emits()/accepts() matching analyse() already does per edge) — not globally per node. A processor with two different outputs routed to two different single consumers is two independent groups of size 1 each and needs no share field on either (this is routing, not competition — no reason to force it through the split machinery).
3. Within one resource-group:
   - size 1: `share` optional, defaults to 1. If provided, must satisfy `0 < share <= 1` (else throw, message includes 'share').
   - size > 1 (true fan-out of one resource): EVERY edge in the group must carry a `share` with `0 < share <= 1`. If any is missing or out of range, throw — and the message MUST include the substring 'fan-out' (this preserves plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's existing CONTROL: two outgoing edges with no `share` field must still throw a message containing 'fan-out', unchanged).
   - Sum the group's shares; if it exceeds `1 + 1e-9`, throw a distinct message naming the node id, the resource, and the sum (e.g. `production: node "x" fan-out shares for resource "y" sum to 1.2, exceeding 1`).
4. feasible()'s flow-forwarding step must multiply by the resolved edge share: `dest[resource] += share * (out[resource] || 0)` instead of today's unconditional `+= (out[resource] || 0)`.
5. Update the header comment (production.mjs:11-15) — it currently states v1 disallows fan-out outright; say what is now true instead, including that the SPLIT is still an input, not something this module chooses.

Gate — plant/test/fanout.selftest.mjs (does not exist yet; this ticket brings it into being), styled like plant/test/production.selftest.mjs (every positive case paired with a CONTROL that must fail; margins and achieved amounts checked against hand-computed numbers, never just truthy — per the standing findings that a self-authored gate certifies absence-of-regression and a checker that fails correct work is worse than none):
 - one source split 60/40 across two sinks with different demands: assert each sink's achieved equals rate*share exactly, and each sink's margin is the hand-computed value.
 - CONTROL: same network, shares summing to 1.2 — throws, message names the resource and the sum.
 - CONTROL: same network, one edge missing `share` — throws, message includes 'fan-out'.
 - a processor with two distinct outputs to two distinct single sinks, neither edge carrying `share` — succeeds exactly as if they were two independent single-edge chains (regression case for point 2 above).
 - a single edge with no `share` field still behaves exactly as full flow — achieved byte-identical to today's behavior (backward-compatibility regression case).

Also run plant/test/production.selftest.mjs unmodified: its existing fan-out-without-shares CONTROL (the unlabelled two-edge fixture) must still throw with a message containing 'fan-out', and every other case in that file — convergence, capacity-capping, cycles, resource-matching, band() — must be untouched, since nothing about single-edge networks changes.

Bounded paths (R3): plant/production.mjs, plant/test/fanout.selftest.mjs — nothing else. Independent (R4): this is the only proposal this turn. Reversible (R6): a failed attempt is a revert of two files, neither deployed by anything else, and no level currently exercises multi-edge networks so nothing live depends on this landing.

This lets a network deliberately waste part of an output (e.g. route 70% and leave 30% unrouted) without erroring, matching production.mjs's existing philosophy of refusing only genuine ambiguity or impossibility, not every underused edge.

beads.title: production.mjs: lift the fan-out restriction via explicit shares
beads.body:
FACTORIO.md's oracle-stack table and the vision both name this as the single most valuable thing left to build: production.mjs v1 refuses fan-out outright, and its own header explains why — 'with fan-out allowed, how much of a source's output goes to which consumer is itself a variable to solve for'. This ticket does NOT ask the oracle to solve for that split (a real LP, out of scope). It asks the network literal to supply the split explicitly, which is enough to turn every future fan-out level from ungradeable into gradeable, exactly as gate 5 itself did for sources/sinks.

Bounded paths (R3): plant/production.mjs, plant/test/production.selftest.mjs. Nothing else.

Design (continues 'Fan-out ticket scoped to explicit-share' and 'Share validation groups by RESOLVED resource, not by node' from memory — R5):

1. An edge MAY carry an optional numeric `share` field, `0 < share <= 1`.
2. In `analyse()`, after resolving each edge's shared resource exactly as today (unknown-node and shared-resource checks unchanged), group a node's OUTGOING edges by (from, resolvedResource) — not by `from` alone. A processor with two different outputs must be able to fan out each output independently without one group's validation touching the other.
3. Within a group of size 1 (today's only legal shape): if `share` is present it must be in (0, 1]; if absent, default to 1. This must reproduce every existing single-edge case byte-for-byte — the whole existing selftest's positive cases (the basic chain, both convergence cases, the capacity-cap case) must keep passing unmodified, since none of them set `share` and all expect share=1 behaviour.
4. Within a group of size > 1 (real fan-out): EVERY edge in that group MUST carry an explicit numeric `share` in (0, 1], or throw `production: node "${from}" splits resource "${resource}" without an explicit share (fan-out)`. Keep the substring 'fan-out' in that message so the EXISTING control in production.selftest.mjs — two edges from one source, neither carrying a share, asserted to throw with a message including 'fan-out' — keeps passing without modification.
5. Sum the group's shares. If the sum exceeds 1 (allow a small float epsilon, e.g. 1e-9), throw `production: node "${from}" over-allocates resource "${resource}" (shares sum to ${sum})`. Do NOT require the sum to equal exactly 1 — a network may deliberately leave part of an output unrouted (see the 'learned' decision above).
6. `outEdges` entries carry the resolved `share` (explicit or defaulted). In `feasible()`'s emission loop, multiply the delivered amount by that share: `dest[resource] += (out[resource] || 0) * share`. `inDegree`/topological-sort bookkeeping is unchanged — it already counts one increment per edge, regardless of share.
7. Update the file's header comment (lines ~9-25) to describe the new explicit-share behaviour in place of the flat 'v1 disallows FAN-OUT' sentence — state plainly that the SPLIT is supplied by the network, not solved for, and that this is a deliberate, narrower feature than a general LP.

New test coverage to add to production.selftest.mjs, in the house style already established (every positive case paired with a CONTROL, every number hand-computed — see the file's own header on why):
 - A source (rate 10, resource x) fanning to two sinks via edges with shares 0.3 and 0.7: hand-calc achieved = 3 and 7, margins computed and asserted against the sinks' demands.
 - CONTROL: same two edges with shares 0.3 and 0.8 (sum 1.1) — throws, message includes 'over-allocate'.
 - CONTROL: same two edges, one with an explicit share and the sibling missing `share` — throws, message includes 'fan-out' (a group is all-explicit or entirely rejected, never a mix with an implicit member).
 - CONTROL (regression, must not need editing): the file's existing two-sink-no-shares fan-out case still throws with 'fan-out' in the message, and its paired single-edge CONTROL still passes.
 - A processor with two distinct outputs (e.g. 'gear' and 'scrap'), where 'gear' fans to two sinks with shares summing to 1 and 'scrap' goes to a third sink via a single edge with no `share` field: assert the 'scrap' edge is unaffected by the 'gear' group's multi-edge validation — this is the resolved-resource, not-by-node grouping rule, and it is the one behaviour most likely to regress silently if implemented per-node instead.
 - A single edge with an explicit share < 1 (e.g. 0.6) and nothing else consuming the rest: assert the sink receives exactly rate*0.6, confirming partial-routing is legal and the unrouted remainder is simply not delivered anywhere (not an error).
 - Re-run (or re-assert unchanged) every existing positive fixture in the file — basic chain, both convergence cases, capacity-cap case, band() cases, determinism check — to confirm byte-identical behaviour with no `share` field present anywhere in them.

[turn 15 — done] Lifted production.mjs's flat fan-out ban and replaced it with explicit-share fan-out: an edge may carry an optional numeric `share` in (0, 1]. analyse() now resolves each edge's shared resource in a first pass (unchanged from before), then groups a node's outgoing edges by (from, RESOLVED resource) rather than by `from` alone, so a processor with two distinct outputs fans each out independently. A group of one edge defaults share to 1 when absent (reproducing every pre-existing single-edge case byte-for-byte, since none of them set `share`), and a group of more than one edge requires every member to carry an explicit share, throwing a message containing 'fan-out' otherwise, or 'over-allocate' if the group's shares sum above 1 (with a 1e-9 float epsilon). feasible()'s emission loop now multiplies delivered amount by the resolved share, so an unrouted remainder (shares summing to less than 1) is simply not delivered anywhere rather than being an error. Also rewrote the file's header comment to describe explicit-share fan-out instead of the old flat prohibition. Added the ticket's full new test coverage to production.selftest.mjs: a two-sink explicit-share split with hand-computed achieved/margin, a CONTROL for shares summing over 1, a CONTROL for one explicit + one implicit sibling in the same group, a CONTROL for a single partial share leaving the remainder unrouted, and a resolved-resource-not-by-node grouping case (a processor with 'gear' fanning to two sinks and 'scrap' going to a third sink unaffected by the gear group's validation). Also renamed the old no-share fan-out block's heading and kept its two existing assertions (including the CONTROL) unmodified, and left every pre-existing positive fixture (basic chain, both convergence cases, capacity-cap case, all band() cases, determinism check) completely untouched — none of them set `share`, so they exercise the new default-to-1 single-edge path and should behave identically to before. NOTE: I have Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, so `node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs` (this ticket's own GATE) could not be executed in-turn. Every new assertion's expected number was hand-traced through analyse()/feasible() as edited (10*0.3=3, 10*0.7=7, margin=min(0.5,1/6)=1/6, 10*0.6=6 with margin (6-5)/5=0.2, gear group 10*0.4=4 and 10*0.6=6, scrap group defaulted-share 10*1=10) and every existing fixture was confirmed to carry no `share` field anywhere, so the single-edge default-to-1 path is a byte-for-byte no-op for them. This is the eleventh class-a/creates-gate-adjacent ticket in a row with this exact structural gap (see the standing finding below) — confidence is high from the hand-trace but it is inference, not execution.

beads.title: Fan-out groups by (from, resolved resource) using nested Maps, not a joined string key
beads.body: Considered keying the group-by step with a single string like `${from}\u0000${resource}` or `${from} ${resource}`, then rejected both: a NUL separator risks the exact NUL-byte-in-source class of bug the ledger already has a dead-end for (a scripted edit that put NUL bytes into a .mjs source and every test still passed), and a space separator could in principle collide if a node id or resource string itself contained the separator character (e.g. from="a b", resource="c" vs from="a", resource="b c"). Used `Map<from, Map<resource, edges[]>>` instead — no string concatenation, no collision risk, and iteration order is still insertion order (from-first, then resource-first-seen-within-that-from), which is deterministic and matches the edges array's original order closely enough that no existing ordering-dependent behavior (e.g. which error fires first) changed for any single-group-per-from case. This only matters when node ids or resource names contain unusual characters, which no current fixture does, but nested maps cost nothing extra and remove the risk entirely.

beads.title: Share validity for a lone (non-fan-out) edge is validated too, not just defaulted
beads.body: The ticket's point 3 says 'if share is present it must be in (0,1]; if absent, default to 1' for a group of size 1 — read literally as also applying if a caller supplies an out-of-range share (e.g. 1.5 or -1 or 0) on a single edge with no sibling. Added that check even though no ticket test case exercises it, because leaving a size-1 group's explicit share unvalidated would silently accept a share > 1 (over-delivering more than the source's actual rate would suggest) or <= 0 (delivering nothing or negative amounts) with no error at all — an inconsistency with the size>1 case, which does validate every member's share range. Reverses cleanly: delete the `else if` branch in the group.length===1 arm if this is judged out of scope.

beads.title: This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — the eleventh ticket in a row with this exact structural gap
beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is `node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs`, a shell command. Same shape as lp-dfad42, lp-138b76, and eight subsequent tickets (production.mjs, level1, band(), level-view withSourceRate/verdictLine, level2, level3, level-view layout, and the throw-message-substring turn). Repeating the standing recommendation an eleventh time because nothing has changed at the source: either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a shell command, or make explicit in the ticket body that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn. Worth escalating past a per-turn note at this point given the count.

beads.title: Standing infra fix: grant Bash (or a narrow test-runner tool) to loop-work turns whose GATE is a shell command
beads.body: Eleven consecutive class-a/creates-gate tickets in the ledger (lp-dfad42 through this one) have named a shell command as their acceptance gate while the executing turn's tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only — no way to run it. Every one of those turns instead hand-traced the expected numbers through the source and reported high-but-unexecuted confidence. That has worked so far because the numbers were chosen to be exact and the traces were careful, but it is inference standing in for verification eleven times running, and the actual gate-running only happens downstream in CI or the judge — which is fine, but nothing in the ticket format currently says so explicitly, so every turn re-discovers and re-reports the same gap. This is not a change to plant/ — it is a change to how loop-work.yml grants tools to a dispatched turn, or alternatively to the ticket template so it explicitly states 'gate execution happens downstream, hand-trace only.' I cannot make this change myself (out of plant/'s bounded paths and out of my tool grant), so this is a class-d finding-shaped proposal rather than an artifact: the fix belongs in the loop's own workflow/config, not in plant/, and someone with visibility into .github/loop/ and loop-work.yml needs to decide whether to grant Bash to gate-bearing turns or to change the ticket template's wording.

beads.title: production.mjs: autoSplit() — closed-form optimal split for the simplest fan-out case (direct source→sinks, provably max-min fair)
beads.body:
Vision priority 1 calls fan-out 'the ceiling, and the real puzzle' and quotes production.mjs's own former header: 'how much of a source's output goes to which consumer is itself a variable to solve for.' Turn 15 (lp-34239d, done) built the prerequisite the vision asked for first — the network literal can now SPECIFY a split via explicit per-edge `share`, and feasible() computes it correctly — but explicitly scoped OUT the actual solving: 'An optimizer that searches over shares is a distinct, later ticket once this lands' (lp-dc4659, in memory). This ticket is that later ticket, scoped to the one sub-case that has a closed-form, provably-optimal answer — not the general multi-hop LP, which stays out of scope for one turn exactly as it did at turn 15.

The sub-case: a node's fan-out group (edges sharing one (from, RESOLVED resource) group, same grouping analyse() already uses) where (a) no edge in the group carries an explicit `share`, (b) every edge's `to` node is kind 'sink', and (c) each such sink has exactly one incoming edge in the WHOLE network (this fan-out edge is its only supply — so its `demand` is exactly what a fair share should cover, not confounded by supply from elsewhere). For that sub-case there is a closed-form optimal split: allocate proportional to demand, `share_i = demand_i / sum(demand_j over the group)`. This is the unique split maximizing the group's minimum margin: margin_i = (S*share_i - demand_i)/demand_i = S*(share_i/demand_i) - 1, so maximizing min_i margin_i means maximizing min_i(share_i/demand_i) subject to sum(share_i) <= 1 — maximized exactly when every share_i/demand_i is equal (moving budget from a higher ratio to a lower one always raises the min until they're equal), which is exactly proportional allocation. Any group NOT matching (a)/(b)/(c) — an explicit share already present, a destination that's a processor, or a sink fed from more than one edge — is left completely untouched; feeding it to feasible() unchanged still throws exactly as today. This keeps the change strictly additive: nothing that works today changes behavior.

Add to plant/production.mjs: `export function autoSplit(network)` — pure, returns a new `{ nodes, edges }` (nodes may be the same reference; edges is a new array; never mutates the input). For each qualifying group, replace its edges with copies carrying the computed `share`; every other edge (including edges in non-qualifying groups) is copied through unchanged. Callers pass the result to feasible()/analyse() exactly as any other network literal — autoSplit does not call feasible() itself and has no knowledge of margins beyond the ratio identity above. Update the file's header comment to note this new function exists and precisely what it does NOT do (solve the general multi-hop case).

Gate (already exists, extend it): node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs. New section 'autoSplit() — closed-form split for the simplest fan-out case':
 - Source rate 100, resource x, two direct sinks demand 30 and 70 (each sink's only inbound edge, no explicit shares). autoSplit fills share1=0.3, share2=0.7 (hand calc: 30/100, 70/100). feasible() on the result: achieved.s1=30, achieved.s2=70 exactly; margin_s1=(30-30)/30=0, margin_s2=(70-70)/70=0 — assert BOTH margins equal 0, the hand-provable signature of the max-min-optimal split (equalized ratios), not just 'feasible'.
 - Same shape, source rate dropped to 60 (infeasible even optimally split): shares stay 0.3/0.7 (proportional to demand, unchanged by feasibility) -> achieved.s1=18, achieved.s2=42 -> margin_s1=(18-30)/30=-0.4, margin_s2=(42-70)/70=-0.4 — assert both margins equal -0.4 exactly, proving the fairness property holds even when short (neither sink is starved to protect the other).
 - CONTROL: same two-sink shape but one edge already carries an explicit share (e.g. 0.5) — assert autoSplit(network) leaves the edges array byte-identical to the input (JSON.stringify equal): a partially-explicit group is never touched, matching analyse()'s existing all-or-none rule.
 - CONTROL: a fan-out group whose second edge targets a processor, not a sink — assert autoSplit leaves it untouched (byte-identical edges) and that calling feasible() on the untouched result still throws with 'fan-out' in the message, exactly as before this ticket.
 - CONTROL: a sink with two incoming edges overall (this fan-out edge plus one more from a different source) — assert autoSplit leaves that group untouched too.
 - CONTROL: a single-edge (non-fan-out) group — assert autoSplit is a complete no-op (byte-identical network), and pass one of the file's existing single-edge fixtures through autoSplit before feasible() to confirm identical achieved/margin to calling feasible() directly.
 - No-mutation check: JSON.stringify of the input network is unchanged after calling autoSplit (same pattern level-view.selftest.mjs already uses for withSourceRate).

Bounded paths (R3): plant/production.mjs, plant/test/production.selftest.mjs. Independent (R4): does not touch level-view.js, any levels/*.mjs file, or index.html — no ordering dependency on the drawLevel proposal below; either can land first or alone. Reversible (R6): autoSplit is a new export nothing existing calls, so a bad attempt reverts cleanly with zero effect on feasible()/analyse()'s existing behavior.

[turn 16 — done] Added autoSplit(network) to plant/production.mjs: a pure function that fills in the missing `share` field for the one fan-out sub-case that has a closed-form, provably-optimal answer — a direct source-or-processor -> sink fan-out, grouped by (from, RESOLVED resource) exactly as analyse() groups them, where every edge in the group carries no explicit share yet, every destination is kind 'sink', and each such sink has exactly one incoming edge in the whole network. Qualifying groups get share_i = demand_i / sum(demand_j), the proportional-to-demand split that is the unique max-min-fair allocation (worked in the ticket and restated in the function's docstring). Every edge outside a qualifying group — explicit share already present, destination not a sink, or a sink fed from elsewhere too — is copied through byte-identical; feasible() on an untouched network behaves exactly as before this ticket, including still throwing on an un-split fan-out. autoSplit never mutates its input (new edges array of new edge objects; nodes reference passed through unchanged) and never calls feasible() itself. Extended plant/test/production.selftest.mjs with a new section covering: the closed-form split and its zero-margin signature on both sides of the fan-out; the same shares surviving an infeasible (starved) source with both sinks margin -0.4 (proving neither is starved to protect the other); and four untouched-CONTROL cases (explicit share already on a sibling edge, a non-sink destination with the feasible() throw re-verified, a sink with a second supplier elsewhere in the network, and a single-edge non-fan-out group including a before/after equivalence check against calling feasible() directly) plus a no-mutation check. Every new number was hand-derived from the demand values in the fixtures (30/100=0.3, 70/100=0.7, 60*0.3=18, 60*0.7=42, resulting margins (18-30)/30=-0.4 and (42-70)/70=-0.4) and checked with the same 1e-12 tolerance pattern the rest of the file already uses.

beads.title: level-view.js: drawLevel must render every outgoing edge, not just the last one per node
beads.body:
level-view.js's drawLevel() builds `next = new Map(level.edges.map((e) => [e.from, e.to]))` (level-view.js:49) — a Map keyed by a node's id, so a SECOND outgoing edge from the same node silently overwrites the first and only one arrow is ever drawn. The comment directly above it (level-view.js:42-44) says why this was believed safe: 'Only the INCOMING side ever fans in — production.mjs v1 caps every node at one outgoing edge.' That comment is now wrong: turn 15 (lp-34239d, done) lifted that cap — production.mjs's analyse()/feasible() fully supports a node fanning one resource out across multiple edges via explicit `share` fields (plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's 'fan-out WITH explicit shares' section). So today the oracle can express a network the renderer silently corrupts: any level with a real fan-out edge would report correct feasible()/margin numbers while drawLevel() draws only the LAST of that node's edges and drops every other one — a visitor would see one arrow and a verdict that doesn't match what is on screen. This was flagged and deliberately deferred at the time (lp-fdd8a1: 'did not pair the fan-out oracle ticket with a level-view.js rendering fix... left for a follow-up turn once the oracle change lands and an actual level needs it') — the oracle change has now landed, so this is that follow-up.

Fix, bounded to plant/level-view.js only:
1. Change `next` to a Map<fromId, Array<{to, share}>> — collect every outgoing edge per node, in `level.edges` order, instead of overwriting.
2. No change to production.mjs, to any levels/*.mjs file, or to drawLevel's column-layout logic (columns are keyed off `incoming`, which is already correct and untouched) — this is exactly and only the outgoing-arrow bug.

beads.title: autoSplit() qualification is judged edge-by-edge inside a group, not group-by-group
beads.body: A group qualifies only if EVERY edge in it independently satisfies (a) no pre-existing share, (b) sink destination, (c) sole supplier of that sink. One disqualifying edge (e.g. one sibling already carrying an explicit share, or one destination being a processor) disqualifies the WHOLE group, not just that edge — matching analyse()'s existing all-or-none rule for explicit shares ("a group is all-explicit or entirely rejected, never a mix", already asserted in the pre-existing CONTROL block). This keeps autoSplit's output always feeding a network that is either fully resolved for that group or fully untouched, never a partial fill that could silently violate analyse()'s own invariant. Reversing this (per-edge partial fill) would need re-deriving what analyse() does with a group half-explicit-half-inferred, which is exactly the ambiguity the existing all-or-none rule was written to avoid.

beads.title: Wire autoSplit() into a level: the first level where a player's placement decision changes who gets fed
beads.body:
autoSplit() (this ticket) and explicit per-edge share (lp-34239d, done) both exist in production.mjs but no levels/*.mjs file uses fan-out at all — levels 1-3 are all single-chain or independently-bottlenecked, never a shared source split between competing sinks. The natural next level: one source, two sinks with different demand, feasible only if the source rate clears the SUM of both demands with the auto-split applied (autoSplit(network) then feasible()) — the player's lever is the source rate (or a future ticket's lever: which sinks are even connected), and losing looks like one sink starved to feed the other, which is the first time a player's own choice (not just a slider) determines who gets shorted. Class-a once written, gated on a new plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs (does not exist yet, so this needs createsGate) that pins the exact achieved/margin numbers the way level1-3's selftests already do. Bounded paths: plant/levels/level4.mjs, plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs — does not touch production.mjs, level-view.js or index.html, so it can land independent of any pending level-view work.

[turn 18 — done] Wrote plant/levels/level4.mjs (LEVEL_4: one source 'ore' fanning out to two sinks 'stockpileA'/'stockpileB' with different demand, 30 and 70) and plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs, the gate this ticket creates. The level's edges carry no explicit share, so feasible(LEVEL_4) alone throws exactly as production.mjs documents for an unsplit fan-out; the level must be passed through autoSplit() first, which fills share=demand/totalDemand for each sink (0.3, 0.7). Shipped at source rate 102 against total demand 100, both sinks land at margin 0.02 ('tight', same texture as LEVEL_1/LEVEL_3). The test pins: the raw-feasible-throws precondition, autoSplit's exact share values, the shipped case's exact achieved/margin numbers, one case per band() (tight/comfortable/slack/infeasible via rates 102/130/200/60), that autoSplit's proportional split makes both sinks share the SAME percentage shortfall while stockpileB (larger demand) loses more ABSOLUTE units than stockpileA when starved, and that neither withSourceRate nor autoSplit mutates LEVEL_4. Did not touch production.mjs, level-view.js, or index.html (only imported their existing exports), matching the ticket's bounded paths exactly. Gate could not be executed in-turn (no Bash) — every number was hand-derived from production.mjs's documented feasible()/autoSplit() algebra and cross-checked against plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's already-passing autoSplit fixture, which uses the identical 30/70 demand split and independently confirms the 'both starve equally' proportional-split property this test also asserts.

beads.title: autoSplit's proportional fan-out does not produce 'one sink starved to feed the other' — it produces equal-percentage, unequal-absolute shortfall
beads.body: The ticket's framing ('losing looks like one sink starved to feed the other') suggested a favor-one-over-the-other dynamic. autoSplit()'s actual formula (share_i = demand_i / totalDemand, proved max-min-optimal in production.mjs's own header, and already exercised by production.selftest.mjs's autoSplit block) gives every sink the SAME percentage shortfall when supply is short — nobody is favored, and this turn's CONTROL A explicitly asserts marginA === marginB at rate 60. What DOES differ between the two sinks is the ABSOLUTE unit count: stockpileB (demand 70) loses 28 units to stockpileA's 12 at the same rate cut, simply because it demands more. I built the level and its test around this corrected, actually-true property rather than the ticket's literal wording. Reversal condition: if a future ticket wants a real favor-one-sink lever, it needs explicit per-edge share (already supported, see production.selftest's 'fan-out WITH explicit shares' block) on a level whose network is NOT run through autoSplit — that is a different, not-yet-built level.

beads.title: LEVEL_5: the first level where the player's own explicit-share choice decides who gets fed, not a formula
beads.body:
LEVEL_4 (turn 18-19, done) uses autoSplit() to divide a source's output automatically -- proportional to demand, no player choice in HOW it splits, only in the shared rate. Vision priority 1 calls the actual decision 'splitting a shared output between competing consumers... the genre's central decision', and that decision is exactly what autoSplit removes from the player's hands. production.mjs already supports the other half of fan-out -- an explicit per-edge `share` the network literal sets directly (plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's 'fan-out WITH explicit shares' section, landed turn 15/lp-34239d) -- and no level exercises it as a player lever. This ticket is that level: the first one where the player's OWN choice, not a formula, decides which of two competing sinks gets fed.

Shape: one source `well` (resource water, rate 100) fanning out over two EXPLICIT-share edges to two sinks, `fieldA` (demand 30) and `fieldB` (demand 50):

  well --share shareA--> fieldA
  well --share (1-shareA)--> fieldB

Because the two shares are defined as `shareA` and `1 - shareA`, they always sum to exactly 1 -- the network is always LEGAL (production.mjs's 'over-allocate' refusal is only reachable above sum 1; the (0,1] per-edge bound is only violated at the extremes shareA=0 or shareA=1, both outside this level's intended play range) -- so this level is entirely about the FEASIBILITY trade-off (who gets shorted), not the illegal-network throw, which stays untouched and out of scope.

achievedA = 100*shareA, achievedB = 100*(1-shareA). Both sinks are simultaneously fed (ok=true, no deficits) exactly when shareA is in [0.30, 0.50] -- a real window, not a knife-edge: shareA >= 30/100 = 0.30 (else fieldA short) and shareA <= 0.50 (else fieldB short, since 1-shareA must be >= 50/100 = 0.50). The optimal point (equal margins on both sinks, matching autoSplit's own proportional-fairness proof already in production.mjs's docstring) is shareA = 30/80 = 0.375, giving margin 0.25 on both sinks (band 'comfortable').

Ship LEVEL_5 with shareA = 0.30 -- the LOW edge of the valid window: fieldA is exactly met (margin 0) and fieldB has slack (margin 0.4), overall margin 0, band 'tight' -- the same 'opens feasible, barely' texture LEVEL_1/LEVEL_3/LEVEL_4 all ship with. A future slider nudged up toward fieldB improves both sinks up to 0.375, then trades fieldA's margin away again past it; push far enough past 0.50 and fieldA keeps gaining while fieldB starves, and dropping below 0.30 starves fieldA while fieldB gains -- two distinct, opposite failure directions from one lever, which no existing level has (LEVEL_1/2/3 each have exactly one failure direction; LEVEL_4's failure is symmetric, not directional).

Write plant/levels/level5.mjs exporting:
  - `LEVEL_5` -- the network above, shares literal (0.3, 0.7), matching the shape and header-comment style of levels/level1.mjs through level4.mjs (explain the shape and the hand-computed shipped numbers).
  - `withShareA(level, shareA)` -- a level-local helper (do NOT add this to level-view.js -- lp-bc6980 is an open, ready ticket editing that exact file's edge-handling logic right now, and touching it here risks a collision; level2.mjs's SMELTER_OPTIONS is the precedent for a level keeping level-specific helpers in its own module rather than the shared one). Returns a new level object with the edge whose `to` is `fieldA` given `share: shareA` and the edge whose `to` is `fieldB` given `share: 1 - shareA` (matched by the edge's `to` field, not array position), every other field and node byte-identical, input never mutated -- same contract as `withSourceRate`/`withProcessorCapacity` in level-view.js.

Gate (does not exist yet -- creates it): node plant/test/level5.selftest.mjs, mirroring level4.selftest.mjs's house style (every number hand-computed, every positive case paired with a CONTROL, a no-mutation check). Required cases:
  1. Shipped LEVEL_5 (shareA=0.3): ok=true, achieved.fieldA===30, achieved.fieldB===70, margin===0 (hand calc: min((30-30)/30, (70-50)/50) = min(0, 0.4) = 0), band(margin)==='tight'.
  2. withShareA(LEVEL_5, 0.5) (the other window edge): ok=true, achieved.fieldA===50, achieved.fieldB===50, margin===0, band==='tight'.
  3. withShareA(LEVEL_5, 0.375) (the fair-split optimum): ok=true, achieved.fieldA===37.5, achieved.fieldB===62.5, marginA===marginB===0.25 (assert equality, the max-min-fair signature), overall margin===0.25, band==='comfortable'.
  4. CONTROL -- withShareA(LEVEL_5, 0.2) (favoring fieldB too far): ok===false, exactly one deficit naming 'fieldA', achieved.fieldA===20, margin===(20-30)/30===-1/3, band==='infeasible'; assert fieldB is NOT short (achieved.fieldB===80 >= demand 50).
  5. CONTROL -- withShareA(LEVEL_5, 0.6) (favoring fieldA too far): ok===false, exactly one deficit naming 'fieldB', achieved.fieldB===40, margin===(40-50)/50===-0.2, band==='infeasible'; assert fieldA is NOT short (achieved.fieldA===60 >= demand 30).
  6. No-throw invariant: for shareA in {0.05, 0.3, 0.375, 0.5, 0.95}, feasible(withShareA(LEVEL_5, shareA)) does not throw (shares always sum to exactly 1, always legal) -- a direct check that this level, unlike LEVEL_4's autoSplit path, never needs a try/catch.
  7. No-mutation: withShareA(LEVEL_5, x) leaves LEVEL_5 itself byte-identical (JSON.stringify unchanged), matching every other level's own no-mutation case.

Bounded paths (R3): plant/levels/level5.mjs, plant/test/level5.selftest.mjs only -- no change to production.mjs, level-view.js, index.html or any other levels/*.mjs file. Independent (R4): does not touch level-view.js (deliberately, see above) so it has no ordering dependency on lp-bc6980, and does not touch index.html so wiring it into the page is a separate, later ticket (the same two-step pattern LEVEL_4 itself used: lp-b8af72 built the level+gate first, lp-194a16 wired it in afterward). Reversible (R6): two new files nothing else imports yet; a bad attempt deletes cleanly.

[turn 20 — done] Wrote plant/levels/level5.mjs (LEVEL_5, withShareA) and plant/test/level5.selftest.mjs exactly as specified in the ticket. LEVEL_5 is one source (well, water, rate 100) fanning out over two explicit-share edges to two sinks (fieldA demand 30, fieldB demand 50), shipped at shareA=0.3 (fieldA margin 0, fieldB margin 0.4, overall band 'tight'). withShareA(level, shareA) returns a new level with the fieldA edge's share set to shareA and the fieldB edge's share set to 1-shareA, matched by the edge's `to` field, never mutating the input -- kept local to level5.mjs rather than added to level-view.js to avoid colliding with lp-bc6980's open edit to that file. The selftest covers all seven cases the ticket names: the shipped state, the other window edge (shareA=0.5), the fair-split optimum (0.375, equal margins, band comfortable), two CONTROLs (0.2 and 0.6, each starving exactly one named sink while the other stays fed), a no-throw sweep across five shareA values, and a no-mutation check. Every computed (multiplied/divided) value is compared with an epsilon tolerance rather than strict equality -- floating-point multiplication of decimals like 0.3*100 is not guaranteed to land on an exact double, and level4.selftest.mjs's own house style already avoids strict equality for exactly this reason. Only literal, non-computed property reads (LEVEL_5's own stored 0.3/0.7 shares) use strict ===. No Bash was available in this turn -- see the standing recommendation below -- so the gate itself was not executed; every number was hand-traced against production.mjs's feasible() algorithm (documented top of that file, read in full before writing) and cross-checked against the ticket's own worked numbers.

beads.title: production.mjs's own documented 'zero sinks is vacuously feasible' branch has zero test coverage -- close it
beads.body:
production.mjs's header for `feasible()` documents a branch nothing in plant/test/production.selftest.mjs exercises: 'A network with no sinks is vacuously feasible and reports margin 0 (no sink to have headroom over) -- not exercised by any ticket case, recorded as a decision rather than left to fall out silently' (the `if (margin === Infinity) margin = 0;` line in feasible()'s margin loop). That sentence is itself an admission of a coverage gap: the code path exists, is reachable, and is completely untested -- exactly the kind of documented-but-unverified behavior that regresses silently the next time someone touches feasible()'s margin loop, because nothing would fail.

Add to plant/test/production.selftest.mjs (gate already exists, extend it -- this is class-a with no new gate needed) a new section, 'a network with no sinks at all is vacuously feasible, not an error':

  1. A single source, no other nodes, no edges: `{ nodes: [{ kind: 'source', id: 'src', resource: 'iron', rate: 10 }], edges: [] }`. Assert `feasible()` does not throw (one node, empty edges, topological sort trivially succeeds). Assert `result.ok === true`, `result.margin === 0` (not `Infinity`, not `NaN` -- the exact fallback value), `result.deficits.length === 0`, and `JSON.stringify(result.achieved) === '{}'` (achieved is only ever populated by walking sink nodes in the topological loop, and there are none).
  2. CONTROL, a second shape that also has zero sinks but is not degenerate -- a source feeding a processor that feeds nothing further: `{ nodes: [{kind:'source',id:'src',resource:'iron',rate:10}, {kind:'processor',id:'p',inputs:[{resource:'iron',rate:1}],outputs:[{resource:'gear',rate:1}],capacity:5}], edges: [{from:'src',to:'p'}] }`. Assert the same three facts (`ok===true`, `margin===0`, `deficits.length===0`) to prove the vacuous branch is about the ABSENCE OF SINKS specifically, not about a trivially empty network -- a one-node CONTROL alone could not distinguish 'no sinks' from 'nothing happens at all'.
  3. Cross-check against the already-tested `band()`: assert `band(result.margin) === 'tight'` for case 1 -- margin 0 falls in band()'s already-pinned `[0, tight)` bracket (the file's existing band() section already asserts the 0.02 level-1 margin is 'tight'), so this is a real cross-check against already-passing code, not a new assumption about where 0 belongs.

Bounded paths (R3): plant/test/production.selftest.mjs only -- no change to production.mjs itself (the behavior already exists and is correct per its own docstring; this ticket only closes the coverage gap the docstring names). Independent (R4): does not touch level5.mjs, level-view.js, or index.html -- no ordering dependency on any other proposal in this batch. Reversible (R6): pure test addition; a bad attempt reverts one file with zero effect on any passing behavior.

beads.title: index.html wiring-presence gate for LEVEL_1/2/3 -- the same check LEVEL_4 already has, extended to the other three

Write plant/test/index-levels123-wiring.selftest.mjs, same technique as index-level4-wiring.selftest.mjs (fs.readFileSync of index.html as text, no DOM/jsdom, substring/regex assertions) -- this is a real, explicitly-declared gate, not a placeholder around a class-a+createsGate ticket. I deliberately did not propose a sixth level, placement-in-a-pocket work (foam/ is out of this loop's reach per vision.md's own 'what does not matter' list), or generalizing autoSplit's closed form to processor destinations — that last one needs a real max-min-fair proof for a case that isn't obviously optimal by proportional allocation, and forcing it into one turn risked exactly the kind of confidently-wrong general conclusion vision.md warns the loop has drawn before.

beads.title: Did not propose extending autoSplit() to processor destinations
beads.body: autoSplit()'s proportional-to-demand split is proven max-min-optimal for fan-out into sinks (production.mjs's own docstring works the proof). The analogous case for fan-out into competing PROCESSORS is not the same proof — a processor's achieved output depends on its OTHER inputs too, so proportional-to-capacity isn't obviously optimal, and getting that wrong in an unattended turn is the 'wrong general conclusion' failure mode this project has hit before (the 22-degree naive-placement trap, the acos precision bug). beads.title: Pin production.mjs's zero-sink vacuous-feasibility branch in production.selftest.mjs
beads.body:
production.mjs's feasible() docstring (around the `margin` bullet, just above the function) explicitly documents: 'A network with no sinks is vacuously feasible and reports margin 0 (no sink to have headroom over) — not exercised by any ticket case, recorded as a decision rather than left to fall out silently.' That is a real, distinct code path — the `if (margin === Infinity) margin = 0;` reset at the bottom of feasible() only fires when the loop over sinks never runs at all — and it currently has zero test coverage in plant/test/production.selftest.mjs.

This is NOT the kind of coverage-matrix padding the vision explicitly warns against (see lp-dff7a6's finding: 'a coverage matrix whose axes the implementation does not distinguish'). The zero-sinks branch and the normal branch are genuinely different code paths in feasible() — one runs the sink loop and computes a real min(), the other skips it entirely and resets to 0 — so a test distinguishing them is closing a real gap, not relabeling one behaviour twice.

BOUNDED PATHS (R3): plant/test/production.selftest.mjs only. Do not touch production.mjs itself — the behaviour is already implemented and documented; only its test coverage is missing.

WHAT TO ADD: a new console.log-headed block (matching this file's existing house style — every check named via the `ok()` helper already defined at the top of the file) with:
1. A network with a source and a processor but NO sink node at all (e.g. reuse the shape of an existing fixture in this file, drop its sink, and drop the edge into it) fed to `feasible()`. Assert: `r.ok === true`, `r.deficits.length === 0`, and `r.margin === 0` EXACTLY (not just `>= 0` — the reset is a hard assignment, not a computed minimum, so pin the exact value per this file's existing 'known-answer, not truthiness' convention).
2. `band(r.margin) === 'tight'` — band(0) falls in the `0 <= margin < tight(0.15)` branch, so this also pins that the zero-sinks case reads as 'tight' rather than something misleadingly cheerier like 'slack'.
3. A CONTROL, per this file's existing pattern of pairing every positive with one: the SAME node/edge shape but with a sink added back in and demand set so margin is clearly nonzero (e.g. reuse an already-hand-verified fixture elsewhere in this file) — showing the zero-margin result above is specific to having no sinks, not a bug that would fire on any network.

R5 memory this carries: production.mjs:210's own comment already names this gap; this ticket exists to close exactly the gap that comment names, nothing broader.
