beads.title: Planning run 2026-08-05T09:50:29Z
beads.body:
A plan seat was staffed because the ready queue was starved. Output: proposals, born proposed, awaiting human promotion.

[turn ? — done] Read vision.md, FACTORIO.md, production.mjs, level-view.js, index.html and every levels/*.mjs + test/*.mjs to find work that is fresh (not already ready/blocked/proposed), inside plant/, and not one of the three categories that have been repeatedly rejected-by-review without a recorded reason: new straight-line/fan-out levels, placement-legality modules, and cosmetic UI. That ruled out a lot of the obvious next steps, since fan-out (vision item 1) already has levels 4 and 5 shipped and wired, and placement-in-a-pocket (item 2) already has lp-39d6e7 ready. What survived is a confirmed, reachable-in-play correctness bug: level-view.js's verdictLine() only ever reports v.deficits[0], so on LEVEL_4 (the only shipped level whose CONTROL fixture already proves two simultaneous deficits, at the ore4 slider's own minimum of 60) a player who breaks it all the way sees a verdict describing only one of the two starved sinks, even though drawLevel() correctly reddens both boxes. That is exactly the kind of gap the vision's playability bar cares about most: the refusal a player provoked has to be legible, and right now it silently drops half of it. One proposal, tightly scoped, plus one ask about whether the fan-out work already shipped satisfies vision item 1 or whether the general multi-hop LP is still wanted.

beads.title: verdictLine()'s fail path drops every deficit but the first — LEVEL_4 already proves it's reachable
beads.body: level-view.js's verdictLine() fail branch reads `const d = v.deficits[0]` and builds its entire message from that one entry. plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs's 'CONTROL A' fixture (ore rate 60 — which is literally the ore4 slider's own min= in index.html, so a player can reach it with one drag) already asserts `r.deficits.length === 2` with both stockpileA and stockpileB short by different absolute amounts. drawLevel()'s box-coloring (`verdict.deficits.some(...)`) correctly reddens both boxes in this state, but the verdict text under them names only one. LEVEL_5 never triggers this (its whole design, per level5.mjs's header, keeps the two sinks' failure windows disjoint so only one is ever short at a time), which is probably why this has gone unnoticed — it needs LEVEL_4 specifically and the slider dragged to its floor.

beads.title: Scoped this turn away from a new level, placement-legality, and cosmetic UI
beads.body: vision item 1 (fan-out) already has levels 4 and 5 shipped and wired (production.mjs's autoSplit()/explicit-share, landed turns 15-16 per the ledger), and vision item 2 (placement in a real pocket) already has lp-39d6e7 ready plus lp-f25c2f unblocking something upstream of it — proposing either would duplicate open work. A sixth level was the other obvious direction but lp-c436ee is a still-open, unanswered ask asking specifically why LEVEL_4/5/6 proposals were rejected-by-review with no reason recorded, and FINDING logs several near-duplicate level and placement-legality proposals going unpromoted across turns — adding another one now would be repeating a pattern the operator hasn't weighed in on yet. verdictLine's gap is none of those three: it's a bug in code that already shipped, in a file with an existing gate, independent of every ready/blocked ticket.

beads.title: Does explicit-share fan-out (levels 4 & 5, shipped) satisfy vision item 1's 'the real puzzle', or is the general multi-hop LP still the priority?
beads.body:
vision.md's item 1 was written against production.mjs v1, which refused fan-out outright — the file explicitly says 'every level so far is a straight line... by force, not by choice.' Since then (per the ledger: turns 15-16, lp-34239d and follow-ons) production.mjs grew explicit-share fan-out and autoSplit()'s closed-form proportional split, and levels 4 and 5 shipped exercising both — one automatic, one player-set. But production.mjs's own header is explicit that this is 'a deliberate, narrower feature than a general LP': a fan-out into PROCESSORS, or a sink fed by MORE than one supplier, still 'needs a real linear program over the whole network and is deliberately left alone.' That's a multi-turn build, not a one-turn ticket, and nobody has picked it up — possibly because it's genuinely too large for the current per-turn shape, possibly because levels 4/5 already answered the vision's concern and nobody said so.

DO: Open plant.minomobi.com and play levels 4 and 5 for a couple of minutes — level 4's automatic proportional split, level 5's player-set share slider between fieldA and fieldB.

WATCH FOR: Whether deciding where a shared output goes feels like 'the genre's central decision' vision item 1 names, or whether it still feels like tuning a slider toward a formula the game already knows the answer to.

SO THAT: If it reads as satisfying item 1: future turns should stop budgeting toward the general multi-hop LP and move fully to placement/gate 6 work instead, and vision.md's item 1 should be marked closed the same way gate 5 and levels 1-3 already are. If it does NOT: the next several turns need to start actually budgeting toward the general LP as a multi-turn arc (starting with, e.g., just the 'fan-out into processors with a single downstream sink each' sub-case) rather than continuing to look for more closed-form autoSplit() special cases one ticket at a time.

beads.title: verdictLine() must report every sink that fell short, not just v.deficits[0]
beads.body:
BUG, CONFIRMED REACHABLE IN PLAY. plant/level-view.js's verdictLine() fail-path is:

  const d = v.deficits[0];
  return d ? `✗ ${d.sinkId} wanted ${d.demand} ${d.resource} and got ${d.achieved}. Short by ...` : '✗ infeasible';

This only ever describes the FIRST entry in v.deficits. plant/production.mjs's feasible() can return more than one deficit — plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's convergence and fan-out blocks exercise this, and plant/test/level4.selftest.mjs's own 'CONTROL A — rate dropped to 60' fixture asserts `r.deficits.length === 2` (both stockpileA and stockpileB short, by different absolute amounts — see that file's comment 'the new lesson'). Rate 60 is not a synthetic edge case: it is exactly the minimum of the ore4 `<input type="range" min="60" ...>` slider wired into plant/index.html for LEVEL_4, so a visitor who drags that slider all the way down reaches this state during ordinary play. drawLevel() already handles multiple deficits correctly — `verdict.deficits.some((d) => d.sinkId === n.id)` reddens EVERY starved sink's box, not just one — so the diagram and the verdict text visibly disagree: two red boxes, one sentence.

This is squarely the vision's playability bar: 'an intention they formed, acted on, and got refused for' has to be a legible refusal, and right now the refusal a player provoked on LEVEL_4's worst case is reported as half of what actually happened.

SCOPE. Change verdictLine()'s fail branch to describe every entry in v.deficits (LEVEL_1/2/3's single-sink shape is unaffected — for them v.deficits.length is always 0 or 1, so existing behavior and existing test assertions must not change). Do not touch the ok-path's margin-naming (which sink sets the reported margin) — that's a softer, separate question and out of scope here; do not touch drawLevel() or its edge-drawing logic at all (lp-bc6980 is open against that same function right now — this ticket must not collide with it).

BOUNDED PATHS (R3): plant/level-view.js (verdictLine() only), plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs (new assertions).

GATE (R2): node plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs — already exists and already covers verdictLine's ok-path and single-deficit fail-path (see its header on the 'confident lie' risk: index.html renders verdictLine's return value directly, so a drift here is a wrong verdict presented as a right one). Add a new case reusing an inline two-sink, both-short fixture in the same style as its existing 'drawLevel: convergence' block (construct the network locally rather than importing plant/levels/level4.mjs, per that file's own stated independence rule so this ticket carries no ordering dependency on LEVEL_4's module — R4) — assert the returned string names BOTH starved sinks' ids, not just one. Keep the existing single-deficit assertions (level1.selftest.mjs's starved fixture) passing unchanged, and add a control confirming the old truncate-to-one-message shape does not silently still satisfy the new assertions (e.g. assert the string's occurrence count of each sink id, not just `.includes`).

REVERSIBLE (R6): pure string-formatting change to one function; a failed attempt is a revert with no other state to unwind.

MEMORY THIS CARRIES (R5): the level-view.selftest.mjs header's own 'confident lie' framing; lp-a427fe's 6/6-mutation-killed trust in production.mjs's deficits as ground truth; the LEVEL_4 module comment naming 'both sinks fall short... by different amounts' as its entire pedagogical point, which the current verdict text fails to actually say.

[turn 22 — done] Changed verdictLine()'s fail branch in plant/level-view.js to map over ALL of v.deficits instead of reading only v.deficits[0], joining one clause per starved sink into a single sentence (e.g. '✗ stockpileA wanted 5 ore and got 3 (short by 2); stockpileB wanted 8 ore and got 7 (short by 1).'). The v.deficits.length === 0 fallback to '✗ infeasible' is preserved unchanged, and the single-deficit case reduces to the same wording as before (one clause, no join separator visible) so the existing 'fail path: unchanged by this edit' test still passes untouched. Did not touch drawLevel(), the ok-path's margin/band naming, or anything outside verdictLine(). Added one new test block to plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs with an inline two-sink fan-out fixture (source rate 10, explicit shares 0.3/0.7 to two sinks demanding 5 and 8) that reproduces the same 'both sinks short by different amounts' shape LEVEL_4's CONTROL A hits at its slider floor, without importing levels/level4.mjs. Asserts both sink ids, both demands, both achieved values appear, and — as the control against the old truncate-to-one shape — that each sink id's substring occurrence count in the output is exactly 1 (the old code would have produced 0 occurrences of the second sink's id). Could not execute `node plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs` in-turn (no Bash grant); every existing and new assertion was hand-traced against feasible()'s already-proven achieved/deficits algebra (3 = 10*0.3, 7 = 10*0.7, margins -0.4/-0.125) and against the unmodified string-formatting logic for the single-deficit and zero-deficit cases.

beads.title: Multiple deficits are joined with '; ' into one sentence, not rendered as separate lines or a list
beads.body: verdictLine() returns a single string that index.html assigns straight to el.textContent (plain text, no HTML), so a bulleted or multi-line format would either be lost (textContent collapses newlines visually much less than a real list would suggest) or need index.html changed, which is out of this ticket's bounded paths. Joining with '; ' keeps it one sentence, keeps the existing '✗ ' prefix and trailing '.' from the single-deficit case, and requires no caller change. Reversal condition: if a later ticket wants deficits rendered as distinct visual rows (e.g. one per starved sink, styled independently), that's an index.html/CSS change and should return a structured value or a pre-joined HTML string from a different function, not overload verdictLine()'s existing plain-text contract.

beads.title: This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — the seventeenth ticket in a row with this exact structural gap
beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is `node plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs`, a shell command this turn cannot run. The new fixture's numbers (3=10*0.3, 7=10*0.7, short-by 2 and 1) are simple enough to hand-verify with high confidence, and the change to verdictLine() is a small, symmetric generalisation of already-proven logic (the single-deficit case is the new code's length-1 special case, unchanged in output). Repeating the standing recommendation because the count keeps climbing and nothing has changed at the source: either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a shell command, or make explicit in the ticket body that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn. Given this is now the seventeenth instance, whoever owns loop-work.yml should treat this as a workflow-level fix rather than a per-turn note.

beads.title: verdictLine()'s ok-path margin is always the GLOBAL min-margin sink, unnamed — a player can't tell which sink is the tight one on a multi-sink level
beads.body:
band(v.margin) and the percentage in verdictLine()'s ok branch describe production.mjs's global `margin` (min over ALL sinks of (achieved-demand)/demand), but the sentence never names WHICH sink that margin belongs to. On a single-sink level (1-3) this is moot — there's only one candidate. On a multi-sink level (convergence/fan-out, e.g. a future LEVEL_4/5) with sinks at different margins, the ok-path sentence reads as if the whole network shares one difficulty, when really one sink is closer to failing than the others and the player has no way to find out which without opening index.html's per-node 'got X' labels themselves. This ticket's scope explicitly excluded touching the ok-path ("do not touch the ok-path's margin-naming... that's a softer, separate question and out of scope here"), so filing it as its own proposal rather than folding it in.

This is a check that does not exist yet, so it's creates-gate: extend plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs with an inline multi-sink fixture where sinks have different margins (e.g. two sinks at margin 0.5 and margin 0.05) and assert verdictLine()'s ok-path names the tighter sink's id, not just the number. class-a is wrong here because there is currently no assertion anywhere that verdictLine's ok-path names a sink at all -- it never has, even for one sink -- so this is new capability, not a regression check.

beads.title: The loop critiqued its own optimal solution for removing the player's decision — no gate could have caught that, the vision did
beads.body:
The best thing this loop has produced, and it is a critique of its own previous turn.

Turn 15 built autoSplit() — the fan-out unlock, a closed-form provably-optimal split for a qualifying subcase, with the exchange argument stated. Turn 16 wired it into level 4. Correct work, and the mutation testing held (equal-split instead of demand-proportional kills both suites).

Then a later turn read the vision again and wrote level5.mjs, whose header says:

  "LEVEL_4 fans one source out to two sinks, but the split itself comes from
   autoSplit() — proportional to demand, no lever a player can move. Vision
   priority 1 calls the actual decision 'splitting a shared output between
   competing consumers... the genre's central decision', and autoSplit removes
   exactly that decision from the player's hands."

It noticed that its own mathematically-correct solution had automated away the thing the vision said mattered. The optimal split is the right answer to "is this satisfiable"; it is the WRONG answer to "what should the player decide", because a puzzle whose optimum is computed for you is not a puzzle. So level 5 uses the explicit per-edge share instead, and the player chooses.

Measured, the level is real:

  share 0.20/0.80 -> LOSE  fieldA short by 10
  share 0.45/0.55 -> OK    margin 0.100
  share 0.50/0.50 -> OK    margin 0.000
  share 0.80/0.20 -> LOSE  fieldB short by 30

A narrow winnable band with a DIFFERENT failure on each side. Err toward A and B starves; err toward B and A starves. That is a decision with consequences in both directions, which is what makes it a choice rather than a slider with one wrong end.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE LEVEL. Every safeguard in this system is aimed at catching work that is WRONG. Nothing in it can catch work that is correct and beside the point — the gate passes, the judge scores it, the deploy publishes it. autoSplit passed everything and still moved away from the goal.

What caught it was not a gate. It was an agent re-reading the operator's stated intent and noticing a conflict between that intent and an artefact the system had already accepted. That is the vision file doing the one job no gate can do, and it is the strongest evidence so far that the steering channel is load-bearing rather than decorative.

beads.title: Every seat's push loop died on a conflict in a GENERATED file — three stalls in five hours, and the retry was a spin not a retry
beads.body:
The five-hour run stalled three times and all three were the same thing. The last one is the clearest: at 10:05 the planner ran, thought for six minutes, proposed work, applied it to the ledger — and then "Commit the proposals" failed for 31 seconds and exited. Thirty-one seconds is exactly 2+4+8+16, the backoff loop exhausting itself.

THE PUSH LOOP CANNOT SURVIVE A CONFLICT IN A GENERATED FILE.

    git pull --rebase origin "$BRANCH" && git push origin HEAD:"$BRANCH"

loop/data/graph.json is DERIVED from the ledger. Two writers regenerate it from different states, so it conflicts on essentially every concurrent push. The rebase halts with the file unmerged, the `&&` short-circuits, and the next attempt runs `git pull --rebase` again — which now fails immediately because a rebase is already in progress. Four identical failures with sleeps between them. The retry looked like resilience and was a spin, which is the SAME defect as lp-95423f (a bare push retried four times), rediscovered in the layer above.

Fixed in all five committing workflows with the rule this repo already wrote down for exactly this — LOOP-SPRINTS.md's REDO, DO NOT RESOLVE. On a conflict: regenerate the derived file, stage, continue the rebase. Merging a generated file is never right; the generator is the resolution.

WHAT THIS COST, and it is the honest number: three stalls in five hours, and the whole content of at least one full planning turn (six minutes of model time, one proposal set, lost). It also explains why the run appeared to stop dead each time I pushed something — my own commits were the concurrent writer. The operator working alongside the loop was, structurally, the loop's main source of failure.

THE PATTERN IS NOW FIVE INSTANCES DEEP (lp-a4030e, lp-3d6bd4):

  1. the brief taught creates-gate; the outbox had no field for it
  2. the reviewer could not wake the tick on a zero-promote
  3. the worker's propose schema omitted class/gate
  4. the planner could not wake the tick at all
  5. every seat's push loop could not survive a conflict in a generated file

Five different components, one shape: the thing worked and the CHANNEL between it and the next stage could not carry the result. Every symptom was silence — a completed turn whose output went nowhere — because none of these failures throws where anyone is looking.

The generalisable rule, stated as sharply as I can: IN A SYSTEM WHOSE COMPONENTS COMMUNICATE THROUGH ARTEFACTS, THE ARTEFACTS ARE THE SYSTEM. Every one of these bugs was in a seam, not in a component, and every component's own tests passed throughout. A test suite that covers each part and no joint will report perfect health while nothing works end to end.

beads.title: This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — repeating the standing pattern, now at least the eighteenth ticket in a row
beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is `node plant/test/level-view.selftest.mjs`, a shell command this turn cannot run. Confidence is high because: (a) the fix is a mechanical widening of a Map from single-value to array-of-values with no new arithmetic, (b) the new test fixture is copied verbatim from production.selftest.mjs's own already-passing explicit-share block with only node ids matching this file's existing convention, and (c) the existing single-chain and convergence cases in the same file are provably unaffected since every node in both fixtures has out-degree <= 1, so the changed code path (the loop-over-array branch) is never exercised for them -- the Map.get(fromId) for a single-entry array behaves identically to the old single-value lookup, just wrapped in a length-1 for loop. Still inference, not execution. This is now at least the eighteenth class-a/creates-gate ticket in this ledger with this identical structural gap. Repeating the standing recommendation: either grant Bash to turns whose gate is a shell command, or make explicit in the ticket body that gate execution happens downstream (CI/judge) rather than in-turn. Given the count is now approaching twenty, this is squarely a loop-work.yml workflow-level fix, not a per-turn note -- every future turn that repeats this note instead of fixing the workflow is spending a turn's worth of ledger space restating a known problem.

beads.title: Seeded the `next` Map from level.nodes, not from level.edges, so every node gets an array even with zero outgoing edges
beads.body: The old code built `next` purely from level.edges (`new Map(level.edges.map(e => [e.from, e.to]))`), so a node with zero outgoing edges (every sink) simply had no key in the Map at all -- fine for a single-value Map since a missing key and an empty result behave the same at the call site. For the array version I instead seed one entry per node from level.nodes first, then push edges into the corresponding array, so `next.get(id)` never returns undefined for a real node. This costs one extra pass over level.nodes but means the arrow loop's `for (const [fromId, toIds] of next)` also now iterates in level.nodes order rather than edges' first-occurrence order, and iterates every node including sinks that draw zero arrows (an empty inner loop, no cost). Rejected keeping edges-only construction with a `next.get(fromId) || []` fallback at the call site: it works identically but the seeded-from-nodes version means the Map's own shape now matches every other Map in this function (incoming, pos), which are all seeded from level.nodes first -- consistency with the file's existing convention, not a correctness requirement. Reversible in one line if a future turn prefers the edges-only construction; nothing else depends on `next`'s iteration order or its handling of zero-outgoing-edge nodes.

beads.title: Planning run 2026-08-05T11:03:51Z
beads.body:
A plan seat was staffed because the ready queue was starved. Output: proposals, born proposed, awaiting human promotion.

[turn ? — done] Read vision.md's verdict (stop polishing the inspector, make the game) against the current state of plant/production.mjs, plant/levels/*.mjs and plant/test/production.selftest.mjs. Placement-in-a-real-pocket (vision item 2) needs a foamworld pocket that does not exist under plant/, so it is out of this turn's file scope and already queued (lp-39d6e7); fan-out (vision item 1) is directly actionable here. Found that production.mjs's feasible() already accepts an explicit-share fan-out edge whose destination is a PROCESSOR (grouping is by (from, resolved resource), never by destination kind) but no level has ever exercised that path, and that autoSplit()'s closed form explicitly refuses it. Proposed two independent tickets: LEVEL_6, a new level using the already-working processor-fan-out capability to teach a genuinely new decision (splitting shared ore between two recipes with different yields, not just two sinks with different demand); and an autoSplit() extension that lifts its closed form to cover single-in/single-out processor destinations under a capacity-headroom precondition that keeps the existing optimality proof exact. Both are scoped to avoid the inspector, cosmetic UI, and placement work vision.md says does not matter right now.

beads.title: production.mjs already accepts fan-out into a processor, with explicit shares — only autoSplit()'s closed form refuses it
beads.body: analyse()'s groupsByFrom construction groups by (from, resolved resource) and never inspects `to.kind`, so a source can already fan out to two different processors today as long as every edge in the group carries an explicit share. No level has ever exercised that path — LEVEL_4 and LEVEL_5 both fan out directly to sinks. Only autoSplit()'s closed-form auto-fill is restricted to sink destinations (its own docstring and CONTROL say so explicitly).

beads.title: Scoped this turn to fan-out (vision item 1); left placement-in-a-real-pocket alone
beads.body: plant/ has no foamworld pocket — solids.mjs's clearanceNeeded/selfCompatible/pairGap exist but nothing in plant/ generates a real pocket to place a summon into, so vision item 2 cannot be actioned inside this turn's plant/-only file scope. lp-39d6e7 already covers it elsewhere. Also stayed away from the inspector (index.html/view.js) and any cosmetic UI, per vision.md's explicit 'does not matter right now' list.

beads.title: LEVEL_6 ships with explicit per-edge shares, not autoSplit — deliberately independent of the autoSplit-extension ticket
beads.body: Both tickets touch fan-out, but LEVEL_6 never calls autoSplit(), so it does not need the autoSplit extension to land first, at all, or ever (DoR R4). This also matches LEVEL_5's precedent of a player-facing explicit-share level shipping independently of any autoSplit machinery.

beads.title: autoSplit's processor extension is restricted to `from.kind === 'source'`
beads.body: If `from` were itself a processor, the group's total emission R would depend on `from`'s own unresolved inputs — a recursive dependency the existing closed form was never meant to solve. Restricting to a source keeps R statically known (R = from.rate) and keeps the extension's optimality proof exact rather than approximate.

beads.title: Proposed LEVEL_6 as a fresh, independent bead, not a resurrection of whatever was rejected before
beads.body: Ask lp-c436ee (still unanswered) references an earlier LEVEL_6 that was rejected-by-review with no reason recorded, and production.selftest.mjs's header comment already anticipates 'the LEVEL_6 proposal' pattern-matching on error messages — so the name has been a live idea for a while. Neither the old proposal's content nor its rejection reason is visible from here, so this turn designed LEVEL_6 fresh against the current vision and current code, same precedent as re-proposing gate 5 and the fan-out oracle as fresh beads rather than un-rejecting old ones.

beads.title: LEVEL_6: fan-out into two processors with different yields — the first level neither autoSplit nor a straight line can express
beads.body:
New files only: plant/levels/level6.mjs and plant/test/level6.selftest.mjs (does not exist yet, hence createsGate). No other file changes.

Why this is the next level, not a fourth straight line: vision.md item 1 calls 'splitting a shared output between competing consumers' the genre's central decision. LEVEL_4 (autoSplit, proportional-to-demand) and LEVEL_5 (player-set explicit share) both fan a source out directly to two SINKS with no conversion in between — neither can express 'which recipe should get more of the ore', because neither branch converts the resource at a different rate. production.mjs's analyse()/feasible() already accept a fan-out edge whose destination is a PROCESSOR as long as the group's shares are explicit (grouping is by (from, resolved resource), never by `to.kind` — see analyse()'s groupsByFrom construction). No level has ever exercised that path; this is the first.

The shape:
  ore (source, rate 100)
    --share shareA--> smelterA (processor, inputs:[{resource:'ore',rate:1}], outputs:[{resource:'ingot',rate:0.6}], capacity 100)
    --share (1-shareA)--> smelterB (processor, inputs:[{resource:'ore',rate:1}], outputs:[{resource:'ingot',rate:1.0}], capacity 100)
  smelterA -> depotA (sink, demand 24)   -- single edge, no share field (defaults to 1)
  smelterB -> depotB (sink, demand 50)   -- single edge, no share field (defaults to 1)

Both capacities (100) are set so they never bind: worst case supply to either smelter is the full source rate 100, and 100/1 = 100 <= capacity. So this level is purely about the YIELD trade-off (0.6 vs 1.0 ingot per ore), not a capacity bottleneck — LEVEL_3 already owns that lesson.

Valid window: shareA in [0.4, 0.5].
  shareA >= 0.4   (else depotA short: 100*shareA*0.6 < 24)
  shareA <= 0.5   (else depotB short: 100*(1-shareA)*1.0 < 50)
Fair point (equal margins on both sinks): shareA = 4/9 (repeating decimal — compute as a fraction in the test, not a hardcoded literal), giving margin 1/9 on both sinks — still band 'tight' (1/9 < 0.15), a different texture from LEVEL_5's fair point which lands 'comfortable'. That is a new lesson, not a bug: this level's window is tighter.

SHIP at shareA = 0.4 (the low edge, same convention as LEVEL_5):
  supply to smelterA = 40, output = 40*0.6 = 24  -> depotA EXACTLY met, margin 0
  supply to smelterB = 60, output = 60*1.0 = 60  -> depotB margin (60-50)/50 = 0.2
  overall margin = min(0, 0.2) = 0 -> band 'tight'

CONTROL below window, shareA=0.3: smelterA output 18 (short of 24 by 6) -> depotA deficit; smelterB output 70 (margin 0.4, slack) -> overall infeasible, exactly ONE deficit (depotA).
CONTROL above window, shareA=0.6: smelterA output 36 (margin 0.5, slack); smelterB output 40 (short of 50 by 10) -> overall infeasible, exactly ONE deficit (depotB) — the OPPOSITE sink from the first control, mirroring LEVEL_5's 'two distinct and opposite failure directions' lesson, now mediated through conversion rate instead of raw share.

export function withShareA(level, shareA) — same contract as level5.mjs's helper: returns a new level object; the edge whose `to==='smelterA'` gets `share: shareA`, the edge whose `to==='smelterB'` gets `share: 1 - shareA` (matched by `to`, not array position); every other field and node byte-identical; input never mutated. Kept local to level6.mjs, same precedent as level2.mjs's SMELTER_OPTIONS and level5.mjs's withShareA — level-specific helpers live in the level's own module, not level-view.js.

level6.selftest.mjs (house style — every value hand-computed against the numbers above, every case paired with a CONTROL, no slider sweep) must pin: the shipped state's exact achieved/deficits/margin/band; both out-of-window CONTROLs' exact achieved/deficit/margin, including which single sink is short in each; the fair point's equal margins (computed as fractions, tolerance-compared); and that withShareA does not mutate LEVEL_6 (re-stringify check, matching level4.selftest.mjs's convention). Does NOT wire LEVEL_6 into index.html — same deferred-wiring precedent LEVEL_5 set (index-level4-wiring.selftest.mjs / index-level5-wiring.selftest.mjs show wiring lands as its own later ticket).

R5: builds on the FINDING that production.mjs already supports processor-destination fan-out with explicit shares, on FACTORIO.md's fan-out framing, and on the still-open ask lp-15f7f9 — offered as a concrete code answer rather than more prose. R4: independent of the autoSplit-extension ticket proposed alongside it in this same turn; LEVEL_6 uses explicit shares throughout and never calls autoSplit().

[turn 24 — done] Wrote plant/levels/level6.mjs (LEVEL_6 + withShareA) and plant/test/level6.selftest.mjs, the first level exercising fan-out into two PROCESSORS with different yields (0.6 vs 1.0 ingot/ore) rather than into two sinks with no conversion — the shape autoSplit() cannot express because it only auto-fills shares for a direct source/processor-to-sink fan-out, and LEVEL_4/LEVEL_5's straight-to-sink shape never converts the resource. Shipped at shareA=0.4 (depotA exactly met, depotB slack, overall margin 0, band 'tight'). Selftest pins the shipped state, a below-window control (shareA=0.3, depotA short by 6, depotB untouched), an above-window control (shareA=0.6, depotB short by 10, depotA untouched — the mirror-image failure LEVEL_5 established), the fair point (shareA=4/9 computed as a fraction in-test, equal margins of 1/9 on both sinks, band 'tight' — a genuinely tighter window than LEVEL_5's comfortable 0.375 fair point, driven by the yield asymmetry rather than copied numbers), and a no-mutation check on withShareA. Every number was hand-derived from production.mjs's documented feasible() forward pass (source rate * share -> processor scale = min(capacity, supply/inputRate) -> emitted = scale*outputRate -> sink achieved) and cross-checked algebraically (e.g. the fair-point equation 2.5*shareA-1 = 1-2*shareA solved by hand to shareA=4/9). Did not wire LEVEL_6 into index.html — same deferred-wiring precedent LEVEL_5 set (index-level4-wiring.selftest.mjs / index-level5-wiring.selftest.mjs show wiring lands as its own later ticket). No files outside plant/levels/level6.mjs and plant/test/level6.selftest.mjs were touched.

beads.title: autoSplit(): extend the closed-form split to single-in/single-out processor destinations, under a capacity-headroom precondition
beads.body:
Bounded paths: plant/production.mjs, plant/test/production.selftest.mjs — both already exist; the gate command is unchanged, extended with new cases (no new file, no createsGate).

Today autoSplit() explicitly refuses (leaves the whole group untouched) any fan-out group where a destination is not a sink — its own docstring and the existing CONTROL 'a fan-out group whose destinations are not all sinks' pin exactly that refusal. This ticket closes that gap for the one sub-case that still has a provably-optimal closed form: a fan-out from a SOURCE into a mix of sinks (today's case) and single-input/single-output processors that each feed, through nothing else, a sink fed by nothing else.

New qualifying condition, evaluated per group, ALL-OR-NOTHING exactly like today's (a)/(b)/(c) (one disqualifying member leaves the WHOLE group untouched, byte-identical):
  - group-level: `from.kind === 'source'` (see WHY below)
  - each edge already qualifies under (a): no explicit share on it
  - each edge's `to` is EITHER:
    SINK CASE (unchanged): a sink S fed by nothing else in the whole network. effectiveDemand = S.demand, k = 1.
    NEW PROCESSOR CASE: a processor P where:
      * P.inputs.length === 1 and P.outputs.length === 1 (single in, single out — no convergence, no ambiguity about which output matters)
      * P's one output's outgoing edges (in the WHOLE network) form a group of exactly one edge, with no explicit share, whose `to` is a sink S
      * S is fed by nothing else in the whole network
      * HEADROOM: P.capacity * P.inputs[0].rate >= R, where R = the source's rate (`byId.get(from).rate`) — the worst case (share=1) can never make P capacity-bound, so P's scale is always supply/inputRate, never capacity, and the margin stays linear in share
      * effectiveDemand = S.demand / k, where k = P.outputs[0].rate / P.inputs[0].rate

share_i = effectiveDemand_i / sum_j(effectiveDemand_j) — the SAME formula as today with `demand_i` replaced by `effectiveDemand_i`; when every destination is a direct sink (k=1 throughout), the output is byte-identical to today's. The existing equal-margin proof carries over unchanged with demand_i/k_i substituted for demand_i; R cancels out of the share formula itself (only the headroom precondition needs to know R).

WHY `from.kind === 'source'` only: if `from` were a processor, R (what it emits) would depend on `from`'s own inputs, which may themselves depend on shares resolved elsewhere in the network — a recursive dependency this closed form is not meant to solve, matching the file's existing discipline of refusing anything beyond the narrow proven case rather than guessing. A group with a non-source `from` stays untouched, exactly as before this ticket.

Hand-worked case for the selftest — source `ore` rate 100 -> smelterA{inputs:[{resource:'ore',rate:1}], outputs:[{resource:'ingot',rate:0.6}], capacity:100} -> depotA{demand:10}; ore -> smelterB{inputs:[{resource:'ore',rate:1}], outputs:[{resource:'ingot',rate:1.0}], capacity:100} -> depotB{demand:30}:
  effectiveDemand_A = 10/0.6, effectiveDemand_B = 30/1 = 30
  shareA = (10/0.6) / (10/0.6 + 30), shareB = 1 - shareA  (compute both as expressions in the test, not rounded literals)
  supplyA = 100*shareA, outA = supplyA*0.6, marginA = (outA-10)/10
  supplyB = 100*shareB, outB = supplyB*1.0, marginB = (outB-30)/30
  Assert marginA and marginB are equal (within 1e-9) — that is the optimality signature, same check style as the existing autoSplit block's 'margin_s1 equals margin_s2'.

Required CONTROLs (same house style as the existing autoSplit block — each paired, each checked for byte-identical untouched edges via JSON.stringify): (1) headroom violated (lower one processor's capacity so capacity*inputRate < R) -> group left untouched, feasible() on the result still throws with 'fan-out' in the message; (2) a qualifying-otherwise processor has 2 inputs -> untouched; (3) a qualifying-otherwise processor's own output already fans out further (its own group size > 1) -> untouched; (4) the fed sink S has another supplier elsewhere in the network -> untouched; (5) `from` is itself a processor (not a source) feeding an otherwise-qualifying processor destination -> untouched; (6) a mixed group — one edge a direct sink, one edge a qualifying processor — both qualify together, shares computed via the unified effectiveDemand formula and hand-checked; (7) a no-mutation check on the new code path, matching the existing 'autoSplit does not touch its input' block.

R5: builds directly on production.mjs's own docstring and its existing 'not all sinks' CONTROL, and on FACTORIO.md's framing of fan-out as 'the most valuable single thing left to build'. R4: independent of the LEVEL_6 ticket proposed alongside it in this same turn — no level in this turn calls autoSplit() on a processor-destination group, so this can land before, after, or never relative to LEVEL_6 without either breaking.

[turn 32 — done] Extended autoSplit()'s condition (b) so a SOURCE fan-out group may contain single-in/single-out RELAY processors alongside direct sinks, with effectiveDemand = S.demand / k where k = outputRate/inputRate. A relay qualifies only under the full guard list: from.kind === 'source' (so R is a literal), exactly one input and one output, the processor fed by nothing else in the whole network, its single un-shared outgoing edge ending at a sink fed by nothing else, and the headroom precondition capacity*inputRate >= R that keeps the relay supply-bound at share=1 and so keeps delivered rate LINEAR in share. Any failing relay voids the WHOLE group (all-or-nothing); the pre-existing per-edge exclusion behaviour for DIRECT sinks under condition (c) is untouched, and an all-sink group still accepts a processor `from` exactly as before. Two guards are STRICTER than the ticket asked for, and both are recorded as decisions below: the relay itself must be fed by nothing else (the ticket only required this of the sink behind it, but without it P's supply is not R*share and the whole closed form collapses), and the relay's own outgoing edge must not already carry an explicit share. The margin algebra reduces exactly to the existing direct-sink expression with effectiveDemand substituted — the recipe ratio cancels, R cancels out of the share formula entirely, and the existing exchange/max-min argument transfers unchanged; that derivation is written into the docstring. Tests add a main fixture with two DIFFERENT recipe ratios (0.6 and 1.0 ingot per ore), asserting the shares against expressions rather than rounded literals, asserting the two margins are equal AND equal to the closed form R/total-1, and asserting explicitly that the shares are NOT the naive raw-demand-proportional 0.25/0.75 — that naive answer is the single likeliest wrong implementation and it looks reasonable. All seven required CONTROLs are present plus three extra (headroom boundary pinned from both sides at 99.9/100, relay fed from outside, relay output already explicitly shared). HONEST CAVEAT: this turn had Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only and no Bash, so `node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs` was NOT executed. Every number was hand-traced through feasible()'s documented forward pass, and every pre-existing autoSplit assertion in the file was independently re-traced against the new code to confirm zero behaviour change — including the existing 'destinations are not all sinks' CONTROL, which still refuses (now because its processor relays to nothing at all, out-degree 0), and whose comment I updated to say so rather than leaving it silently reinterpreted.

beads.title: Capacities set to 100 on both smelters so LEVEL_6 tests only the yield trade-off, not a capacity bottleneck
beads.body: The ticket specifies capacity 100 for both smelterA and smelterB, high enough that neither ever binds (worst-case supply to either is the full source rate of 100, and 100/1 <= 100). I kept this as specified rather than tightening it, so the level isolates exactly one new lesson — differing conversion yields change how much of a shared input is worth routing where — without reintroducing LEVEL_3's already-covered capacity-bottleneck lesson. Reversed if a future ticket wants a level that combines both a yield trade-off and a binding capacity; that would need a different, tighter capacity value and is a distinct level, not an edit to this one.

beads.title: Fair-point share computed in-test as a literal fraction (4/9), not a rounded decimal
beads.body: level5.selftest.mjs uses a terminating fair-point value (0.375) that can be written as a literal. LEVEL_6's fair point is a repeating decimal, so the selftest computes it as `4/9` in JavaScript rather than truncating to a fixed number of decimal digits — avoiding disguising a derived, non-terminating number as a given one (echoing lp-dff7a6's point about coverage/precision that looks more exact than it is). Reversed if a reviewer prefers a pinned literal with an explicit tolerance comment instead; I judged the fraction more honest about where the number comes from.

beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is 'node plant/test/index-level6-wiring.selftest.mjs', a shell command this turn cannot run. beads.body: analyse() already computes a deterministic topological order to walk feasibility; buildOrder() only exposes it. Keeps the ticket small and the behavior provably identical to feasible()'s internal walk order.

beads.title: CSS fix specified as a shared .lvl-svg class, not six repeated id-selectors
beads.body: A comma-joined six-id selector list would work too, but a shared class is what a seventh level would need anyway, and it lets the gate assert the OLD svg#lvl-scoped rules are gone (proving the fix isn't just additive) as cleanly as asserting the new ones are present.

beads.title: Does a purely topological (non-spatial) construction order count as real progress on gate 6, or is gate 6 meaningless without the pocket geometry?
beads.body:
I'm proposing buildOrder() — exposing production.mjs's existing topological sort as 'a legal construction order' toward FACTORIO.md gate 6. It is honestly only half the problem: it proves dependency order (build the source before what consumes it) but says nothing about whether each build physically FITS where it lands, which needs the pocket/hull work (clearanceNeeded, selfCompatible, pairGap) that lives outside plant/'s files entirely. I can't tell from here whether gate 6 is meant to compose from a non-spatial half plus a spatial half added later, or whether a construction order that ignores space is a distraction that will just get thrown away once the real (spatial) certificate exists.

DO: Read the two-sentence FACTORIO.md gate 6 description again with buildOrder() in mind, and decide: is 'an order that respects dependencies, with placement legality checked separately/later' a sane decomposition of gate 6, or does gate 6 only mean something once a single check does both at once?

WATCH FOR: Whether your instinct is 'yes, and here's what the spatial half should bolt onto' (a shape for buildOrder()'s output that a later placement checker could consume) versus 'no, don't bother — a construction order without space is not a certificate of anything'.

SO THAT: If yes, I (or a later turn) extend buildOrder() toward something a spatial checker can consume once that work lands, and gate 6 becomes an explicit two-layer build. If no, buildOrder() gets dropped or demoted and future turns stop investing in the non-spatial half of gate 6 inside plant/ at all.

beads.title: Export buildOrder(network) from production.mjs — the topological construction order analyse() already computes
beads.body:
Bounded paths: plant/production.mjs, plant/test/production.selftest.mjs only.

Why: FACTORIO.md §2 gate 6 ('the build certificate — a legal construction order exists') is the hard unbuilt gate and vision.md names it as 'where the turns will really go'. production.mjs's internal analyse() already computes a deterministic topologically-sorted node-id list (Kahn's algorithm, documented at production.mjs:168-183) to walk feasibility, but that order is never returned to a caller — feasible() only returns achieved/deficits/margin. Exposing it is the smallest possible first step toward gate 6: a topological order over the dependency graph IS a legal construction order for the non-spatial half of the problem (build a node only after everything it depends on already exists) — it does not attempt the spatial half (does it physically fit where placed), which is out of this ticket's scope and belongs with the placement-in-a-pocket work (lp-39d6e7/lp-f25c2f) tracked elsewhere.

What to build: in plant/production.mjs, add `export function buildOrder(network) { const { order } = analyse(network); return order; }` (or equivalent — the important thing is it reuses analyse() rather than re-implementing the sort, so it inherits analyse()'s exact validation and refusal behavior, including the cycle check, with zero duplicated logic). Do not change feasible()'s existing return shape or any other exported function's signature.

Gate assertions to add to plant/test/production.selftest.mjs (import buildOrder alongside feasible/band/autoSplit):
  - On the file's existing basic chain fixture (source 'src' -> processor 'proc' -> sink 'snk'), buildOrder() returns exactly ['src','proc','snk'].
  - On the file's existing two-source convergence fixture (sources 'a','b' -> processor 'p' -> sink 's', nodes declared in that order), buildOrder() returns exactly ['a','b','p','s'] — hand-traceable from Kahn's algorithm: both sources start with in-degree 0 and are queued in nodes-declaration order (a before b), so a is dequeued first, then b (which is what finally drops p's in-degree to 0), then p, then s.
  - On the file's existing two-node cycle fixture, buildOrder() throws, and the thrown message includes 'cycle' — same wording as feasible() already asserts on the identical fixture, since both go through analyse().
  - Determinism: two buildOrder() calls on the same network literal produce byte-identical arrays (JSON.stringify equal) — same discipline as the file's existing 'determinism' section for feasible().
  - CONTROL: buildOrder()'s returned array length equals the network's node count, on at least one multi-node fixture — guards against a future refactor silently dropping or duplicating an id.

Findings this carries: 'production.mjs already accepts fan-out into a processor, with explicit shares' and the gate-5-built findings establish analyse() as the shared, trusted validation core — this ticket adds no new validation path, only a new view onto the one that exists. R6: a failed attempt only touches these two files and either passes or the existing suite still catches any regression to feasible()/band()/autoSplit().

[turn 27 — done] Added export function buildOrder(network) to plant/production.mjs, placed between analyse() and feasible() with a doc comment tying it to FACTORIO.md gate 6 (the non-spatial half of a build certificate). It does nothing but destructure { order } off analyse(network) and return it — zero duplicated logic, so it inherits analyse()'s exact validation, cycle-refusal, and message wording for free. feasible()'s return shape and every other export's signature are untouched. Added a new test block to plant/test/production.selftest.mjs (imports buildOrder alongside the existing imports) asserting: the basic chain fixture orders ['src','proc','snk']; the convergence fixture orders ['a','b','p','s'] (hand-traced through Kahn's algorithm — both sources start in-degree 0 and queue in declaration order, b is what drops p's in-degree to 0); the two-node cycle fixture throws with 'cycle' in the message; two calls on the same network produce byte-identical JSON (determinism, same discipline as feasible()'s section); and the convergence fixture's buildOrder() length equals its node count (4) as a control against a future refactor silently dropping or duplicating an id.

beads.title: Style levels 2-6's SVG text: the .ln/.ls/.ls.bad rules only ever matched svg#lvl (level 1)
beads.body:
Bounded paths: plant/index.html and plant/test/level-svg-style.selftest.mjs (new) only.

Why: plant/level-view.js's drawLevel() is level-agnostic and stamps class="ln" onto every node's label text and class="ls" (plus "bad" when short) onto every value line, for EVERY level (level-view.js:90-91) — this is the shared renderer used by all six levels. But plant/index.html's <style> block only ever scopes those classes under the selector `svg#lvl` (index.html:63-66), which is level 1's svg id. Levels 2 through 6 (svg ids lvl2..lvl6) get NO font-size and NO fill for .ln/.ls text, and critically no fill for .ls.bad — the red text that is the on-screen signal a sink came up short. This is not cosmetic polish: vision.md's playability bar is 'an intention they formed, acted on, and got refused for', and the refusal's visible proof for 5 of the site's 6 levels currently renders with default (unset) SVG text styling instead of the designed one. Pre-existing, not introduced by any recent ticket — first flagged as a bare FINDING with no bead yet.

What to build: give every one of the six <svg id="lvl">...<svg id="lvl6"> elements (index.html lines ~125, 156, 178, 205, 233, 261) a shared `class="lvl-svg"` attribute (in addition to their existing id — do not remove the ids, other selftests and the JS both key off them). Then rewrite the four existing rules in the <style> block from `svg#lvl { ... }`, `svg#lvl .ln { ... }`, `svg#lvl .ls { ... }`, `svg#lvl .ls.bad { ... }` to the identical declarations under `.lvl-svg`, `.lvl-svg .ln`, `.lvl-svg .ls`, `.lvl-svg .ls.bad` respectively — same property values, selector swapped, so visual output for level 1 is byte-identical and levels 2-6 newly match it. Do not touch svg#view (the inspector's own, unrelated svg) or any other rule.

Gate (new file, plant/test/level-svg-style.selftest.mjs, reads index.html as text via fs.readFileSync, same house style as the index-levelN-wiring selftests — no jsdom):
  - For each of the six ids lvl, lvl2, lvl3, lvl4, lvl5, lvl6: the `<svg id="<id>"` tag's opening tag text contains `class="lvl-svg"`.
  - The <style> block contains all four of: `.lvl-svg {`, `.lvl-svg .ln {`, `.lvl-svg .ls {`, `.lvl-svg .ls.bad {`.
  - The four OLD id-scoped selectors no longer appear verbatim: `svg#lvl {`, `svg#lvl .ln {`, `svg#lvl .ls {`, `svg#lvl .ls.bad {` — proves this is a real rewrite, not additive duplication that could silently diverge later.
  - The declaration bodies are unchanged: the text immediately following `.lvl-svg .ls.bad {` still contains `fill: var(--bad)`, and following `.lvl-svg .ln {` still contains `font: 600 14px` and `fill: var(--fg)` — pins that the fix didn't also change what the styling IS, only what it applies to.
  - CONTROL: `svg#view` still appears in the style block exactly as before (untouched), and the six svg elements keep their original ids intact (id attribute values still present verbatim), so nothing that already depended on those ids (level-view.js's $('lvl2') etc., the six index-levelN-wiring selftests) can have broken.

Findings this carries: level-view.js's drawLevel/verdictLine/withSourceRate are already level-agnostic (so this is a pure index.html/CSS fix, no renderer change needed) and the standing decision to scope away from cosmetic UI — this is deliberately framed as a functional-legibility fix, not decoration, per the reasoning above. R6: a failed attempt only touches index.html's markup/style and a new test file; reverting is a plain file revert.

beads.title: buildOrder() placed textually between analyse() and feasible(), not after autoSplit()
beads.body: Chose to insert the new export immediately after analyse() (which it wraps) and before feasible(), rather than appending it at the end of the file after autoSplit(). Rejected append-at-end because buildOrder() is conceptually a second view onto analyse()'s output, same as feasible() is, so reading the file top to bottom now goes analyse (private) -> buildOrder (thin public wrapper) -> feasible (the main consumer) -> band -> autoSplit, which groups the two direct analyse()-consumers together. This is purely a readability call with no behavioral consequence; a reviewer who prefers strict chronological-by-ticket ordering would reverse it, and that is a one-line diff to move if it matters to someone later.

beads.title: This turn's own gate is unverifiable in-turn — the nineteenth-plus ticket in a row with this exact structural gap
beads.body: Tool grant was Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep only, no Bash, and the GATE is `node plant/test/production.selftest.mjs`, a shell command this turn cannot run. Confidence is high because buildOrder() has zero new logic (it is a one-line destructure-and-return over analyse(), which is already exhaustively proven by feasible()'s existing passing assertions on the exact same fixtures), and all three new fixtures (chain, convergence, cycle) are copied verbatim from blocks already proven correct earlier in the same file rather than newly authored — the only new work is the Kahn's-algorithm hand-trace for the convergence order, done step by step in a code comment. Still inference, not execution. This is now at least the nineteenth class-a/creates-gate ticket in this ledger with this identical structural gap (see the standing recommendation across lp-dfad42, lp-138b76, and roughly seventeen subsequent tickets). Given the count, this is squarely a loop-work.yml workflow-level fix — every turn that re-notes this instead of the workflow being fixed is spending ledger space restating a fact that has been established many times over.

beads.title: Wire buildOrder() into a LEVEL_6 build-certificate demo — the spatial half stays out of scope, order-of-operations is the whole feature
beads.body:
Now that plant/production.mjs exports buildOrder(network) (this ticket), the smallest next step toward FACTORIO.md gate 6 ('a legal construction order exists') that a player can actually see is a level or inspector panel that takes an existing level's network (e.g. plant/levels/level4.mjs or level5.mjs, both already fan-out networks) and renders buildOrder()'s result as an ordered list or numbered overlay on the existing diagram — 'build 1: ore, build 2: smelterA, build 3: smelterB, ...'. This does NOT attempt placement-in-a-pocket (lp-39d6e7/lp-f25c2f territory, spatial fit) — it only visualizes the non-spatial ordering constraint buildOrder() already guarantees: nothing appears before what it depends on. Scope: a new plant/levels/level6.mjs (or an extension to level-view.js's rendering, whichever turn picks it up decides) plus a new test file, since no existing gate covers build-order rendering.

Why this matters now rather than later: vision.md calls gate 6 'the hard one, and where the turns will really go' and this ticket only built the pure-function half. A player-visible artifact is what turns a passing selftest into something a stranger evaluating plant.minomobi.com can actually see working, which is the standing operator ask (bar for playable: something a stranger can act on and get refused/confirmed within 30 seconds).

Acceptance is genuinely undecided — no test for a build-order visualization exists anywhere in the tree yet, so this is creates-gate, not class-a today.

beads.title: Planning run 2026-08-05T12:01:26Z
beads.body:
A plan seat was staffed because the ready queue was starved. Output: proposals, born proposed, awaiting human promotion.

[turn ? — done] Read production.mjs, production.selftest.mjs, level-view.js/its selftest, worker.js, and levels/level4-6.mjs against vision.md's priorities (fan-out is the ceiling; placement-in-a-pocket is item 2) and the current ready queue (lp-f25c2f, lp-b80b67, lp-39d6e7, lp-484b7f, lp-e8d94e, lp-9be387 already cover fan-out-extension, placement, frame-budget, atomic-insert and the cron PAT). With those staffed, I looked for real, narrow, already-gated gaps instead of inventing a seventh level or re-proposing staffed work, and found four: a sink fed directly by two independent sources is legal input to feasible() but has never been asserted correct (only exercised incidentally, unchecked, inside autoSplit's own CONTROL fixture); the zero-sink vacuous-margin path is named as untested in production.mjs's own comment; buildOrder() — gate 6's non-spatial half, shipped turn 20 — has never been run against a network carrying explicit-share fan-out edges, so gate 6 and vision item 1 have never actually touched; and autoSplit()'s per-resource group independence (proven for feasible() by the existing gear/scrap test) has never been checked for autoSplit() itself. One ticket, one file, one existing gate, no new level (none of these need new oracle expressiveness, so per vision's own rule a level isn't the right vehicle for them).

beads.title: Scoped this turn away from a new level, and away from every already-ready ticket
beads.body: The ready queue already covers vision item 1's continuation (lp-9be387, autoSplit into processor destinations), item 2 (lp-39d6e7, placement in a real pocket), gate 7 (lp-484b7f, frame budget), and infra (lp-f25c2f, lp-b80b67, lp-e8d94e). Proposing any of those again wastes a slot; I looked for gaps those tickets do not cover instead.

beads.title: No new level proposed for the fan-in-sink shape, even though it is a genuinely new visual/topological pattern
beads.body: vision.md is explicit: 'the next level should only exist if the ORACLE can express something it could not before.' feasible() already sums a sink's incoming supply across every edge that reaches it (supplyIn accumulates additively per producer in analyse()'s outEdges walk) — a sink fed by two independent sources needs zero new code, only a test proving the already-shipped behaviour. That makes it a coverage ticket, not a level ticket.

beads.title: Bundled four small, related coverage gaps into one ticket rather than four competing proposals
beads.body: All four touch the same file (plant/test/production.selftest.mjs) and the same existing gate; splitting them into separate beads would only invite avoidable path-lease collisions for no independence benefit, since none of the four's assertions depend on another's outcome (each is a fresh fixture, not a shared setup).

beads.title: Did not propose a binding-constraint diagnostic, a fifth/sixth combinatorial coverage matrix, or anything under plant/index.html or level-view.js this turn
beads.body: The binding-constraint diagnostic was explicitly scoped out by a prior turn's decision and nothing here changes that judgement. Combining orthogonal features (e.g. fan-out x capacity-binding) into one test was the exact zero-marginal-value mistake lp-dff7a6 already cost a turn; each sub-case below exercises a genuinely distinct, previously-unexercised code path instead, not a cross-product of already-tested ones.

beads.title: production.mjs coverage: fan-in sinks, the vacuous no-sink case, buildOrder() with fan-out, and autoSplit()'s cross-resource independence
beads.body:
Add four small, independent test blocks to plant/test/production.selftest.mjs (the file is the whole bounded path — no other file may be touched). Each closes a real, previously-unexercised behaviour; none needs a code change to production.mjs, since all four are already-shipped behaviour, only untested.

(a) A SINK fed directly by two independent SOURCE nodes, no processor in between (e.g. src1 rate 6 + src2 rate 4, both edges to sink 's', demand 8 — no shares needed since each source's own single outgoing edge defaults to share 1 and neither is a fan-out group). Assert feasible().achieved.s equals the hand-computed sum (10), margin matches (10-8)/8=0.25, ok is true. Pair it with a CONTROL that drops one source's edge and shows achieved.s equals only the remaining source's rate, short of demand — proving the sum is real addition, not one source silently winning. This is the shape autoSplit()'s own 'sharedSinkNet' CONTROL fixture already builds (production.mjs's autoSplit() docstring condition (c)) but that fixture only asserts autoSplit() leaves the edges untouched — it never calls feasible() on it to check the achieved numbers are actually correct. See production.mjs lines 231-277 (feasible()'s supplyIn accumulation) and the existing 'fan-out WITH explicit shares' and 'a processor with two distinct outputs fans out independently' blocks in production.selftest.mjs for the house style (hand-computed numbers, paired CONTROL, message-content checks where relevant).

(b) A network with ZERO sink nodes (e.g. one lone source, no edges). Assert feasible() returns ok: true, deficits: [], margin: 0 — the exact vacuous case production.mjs's feasible() docstring (lines 220-229) names explicitly as 'not exercised by any ticket case, recorded as a decision rather than left to fall out silently.' This closes that named gap.

(c) buildOrder() called on a network that carries EXPLICIT-SHARE fan-out edges (reuse the exact fixture from the existing 'fan-out WITH explicit shares' block: source 'src' with two edges to 's1'/'s2' at shares 0.3/0.7). Assert buildOrder() returns ['src', 's1', 's2'] (declaration order breaks the ties, same convention as the existing convergence buildOrder test) and does not throw — proving gate 6's non-spatial half (buildOrder, shipped turn 20 per the existing 'buildOrder()' test section) is unaffected by share values, since analyse()'s topological sort only reads edge structure, never `share`. No existing buildOrder test uses a network with any `share` field at all; this is the first time gate 6 and vision item 1 (fan-out) are actually exercised together in the same fixture.

(d) autoSplit() called on a network where ONE 'from' node has TWO independent resource groups from the same source id — one that qualifies for auto-splitting (two sink destinations, no existing share, each fed only by this edge) and one that does not (a single edge to a different resource, or a group that fails a qualifying condition). Mirror the existing feasible()-side 'a processor with two distinct outputs fans out independently' fixture (mill emitting both 'gear' and 'scrap') but adapted to a case where the 'gear' group qualifies for autoSplit and the 'scrap' edge does not (e.g. because it targets a processor, not a sink). Assert the qualifying group's shares are filled with the same demand-proportional formula already pinned elsewhere in this file, and the non-qualifying edge is byte-identical to its input — proving group independence (grouping is per (from, resolved resource), never per node — analyse()'s groupsByFrom construction) holds for autoSplit() itself, not just for feasible(), which is the only place it is currently checked.

Every sub-case follows the file's existing house style: hand-computed expected values in a comment above the assertion, a paired CONTROL where the ticket calls for one, `Math.abs(...) < 1e-9` for float comparisons, `JSON.stringify` equality for byte-identical-input checks. Findings this carries forward: lp-b5b0b1/lp-20c414 (a checker that fails correct work is worse than none — every new assertion here is checked against a value computed by hand, not just truthiness); the repeated FINDING that a self-authored gate certifies absence-of-regression, not presence-of-correctness — these four cases were chosen because the behaviour they check is ALREADY SHIPPED and already relied upon elsewhere (autoSplit's own CONTROL fixture, feasible()'s own docstring), so the risk being closed is a silent behavioural drift, not a speculative future bug.

beads.title: Planning run 2026-08-05T12:09:31Z
beads.body:
A plan seat was staffed because the ready queue was starved. Output: proposals, born proposed, awaiting human promotion.

[turn ? — done] Read vision.md and the graph: both P1 items it names as 'what matters right now' (fan-out's remaining closed-form case, and placement legality in a real pocket) already have open, unstaffed tickets (lp-9be387, lp-39d6e7), as does gate 7 (lp-484b7f) — proposing more work in those lanes this turn would duplicate rather than add. Instead of guessing at the general-LP question already parked behind unanswered ask lp-15f7f9, or re-litigating cosmetic UI that prior turns had rejected without explanation, I read production.mjs, level-view.js, index.html and worker.js end to end looking for a real, currently-undocumented gap that is independent of every open ticket. Found one concretely: index-level4/5/6-wiring.selftest.mjs each say in their own header that 'none of LEVEL_1/2/3's wiring blocks' have an equivalent presence check — LEVEL_1/2/3 have selftests for their own module logic but nothing proving they are actually still wired into index.html the way LEVEL_4/5/6 do. That is a real, load-bearing gap: a regression that silently unwires Level 1, 2 or 3 from the page (the exact class of bug the LEVEL_4/5/6 wiring tests exist to catch) would currently pass every existing gate. Proposed closing it with one bundled test file mirroring the established house style exactly, rather than three near-duplicate tickets, per the standing preference for bundling small related coverage gaps. Second proposal closes a separate, unrelated zero-coverage gap: plant/worker.js (the /health endpoint and the ASSETS pass-through) has never had a selftest, despite being exactly the kind of site-health surface the top-level CLAUDE.md calls out ('the health probe failed for two minutes... masked by continue-on-error' is a standing finding about exactly this class of gap going unnoticed). Both proposals are read-only against the files they gate, touch only new test files under plant/test/, and are independent of each other and of every open ticket.

beads.title: Did not re-propose fan-out extension, real-pocket placement, or frame-budget work
beads.body: lp-9be387, lp-39d6e7 and lp-484b7f already sit open and unstaffed, covering vision items 1, 2 and gate 7 respectively. beads.title: Scoped this turn to a documented, independent coverage gap instead of cosmetic UI or a new level
beads.body: index-level4/5/6-wiring.selftest.mjs each state in their own header that LEVEL_1/2/3 have no equivalent wiring check — a fact stated in shipped code, not inferred. Closing it is small, bounded, and does not touch anything a sibling proposal or an open ticket depends on. Deliberately avoided the svg#lvl CSS-styling gap (prior turns record it as rejected-by-review with no reason given, per the graph's own finding) and avoided a seventh level (vision.md is explicit: a new level only earns its place if the oracle can express something it couldn't before, and neither of these gaps changes what the oracle can express).

beads.title: Bundled Level 1/2/3 wiring into one new test file, not three
beads.body: Matches the graph's own precedent ('Bundled four small, related coverage gaps into one ticket rather than four competing proposals') and the existing per-level wiring files are already near-duplicates of each other in structure — three separate tickets here would just be the same regex-presence-check pattern copy-pasted three times with three review cycles instead of one.

beads.title: Close the documented LEVEL_1/2/3 index.html wiring-coverage gap
beads.body:
index-level4-wiring.selftest.mjs, index-level5-wiring.selftest.mjs and index-level6-wiring.selftest.mjs each open with the same admission: 'index.html has no DOM/browser test today — none of LEVEL_1/2/3's wiring blocks do either.' That is still true. LEVEL_1/2/3 each have their own module selftest (level1/2/3.selftest.mjs) proving the level DATA is correct, but nothing proves index.html still actually imports each level, threads it through withSourceRate/withProcessorCapacity, calls feasible(), and renders via drawLevel()/verdictLine() into the right DOM ids — the exact class of regression (an edit that silently unwires a level from the page while its own module test keeps passing) the LEVEL_4/5/6 wiring tests exist to catch, and that LEVEL_1/2/3 are currently unprotected against.

Build plant/test/index-level123-wiring.selftest.mjs, matching the house style of the three existing index-level*-wiring.selftest.mjs files exactly: read plant/index.html as text with node:fs (no DOM, no headless browser — say so in the header, same disclaimer the existing three files carry), then assert by regex/substring for each of the three levels:
  Level 1 — imports LEVEL_1, feasible, drawLevel, verdictLine, withSourceRate, withProcessorCapacity from './level-view.js'; a slider with id="ore" wired to an 'input' handler that redraws; svg mount id="lvl" and verdict mount id="lvlVerdict"; a reset control id="oreReset" wired to a 'click' handler.
  Level 2 — imports LEVEL_2_BASE, SMELTER_OPTIONS from './levels/level2.mjs'; button container id="lvl2Btns" wired to a 'click' handler; svg mount id="lvl2", verdict mount id="lvl2Verdict".
  Level 3 — imports LEVEL_3 from './levels/level3.mjs'; two sliders id="miner" and id="smelter3" each wired to an 'input' handler; svg mount id="lvl3", verdict mount id="lvl3Verdict"; reset control id="lvl3Reset" wired to a 'click' handler.
For every level, also assert the block calls feasible(...) and renders via drawLevel(...)/verdictLine(...), same shape as the existing three files' 'the split network is graded by feasible() and rendered like every other level' section.

Bounded paths: plant/index.html (read only — this ticket adds no wiring, it only proves the existing wiring is present) and plant/test/index-level123-wiring.selftest.mjs (new). Independent of every open ticket (R4) — it asserts against index.html as it stands today, with no dependency on lp-9be387 or lp-39d6e7 landing first. Reversible (R6): a failed attempt is a new test file that either doesn't exist or is deleted; nothing else changes.

beads.title: First selftest for plant/worker.js — the /health endpoint and the ASSETS pass-through
beads.body:
plant/worker.js is the only file under plant/'s bounded paths with zero test coverage in the existing suite (it appears in no plant/test/*.selftest.mjs). It is small (fetch(request, env) with one branch for /health and a pass-through), but it is exactly the kind of surface the top-level CLAUDE.md calls out as this branch's whole purpose ('site health: deploys work, pages load, workers respond') and the standing finding 'the health probe failed for two minutes after the site was live — one missing space, masked by continue-on-error' is a direct instance of this class of gap going unnoticed until it was live. worker.js's own header says the /health endpoint deliberately asserts more than liveness — that it can actually serve index.html — because 'a worker that is up and serving nothing is the failure this repo keeps rediscovering'; nothing currently proves that logic does what its comment claims.

Build plant/test/worker.selftest.mjs. worker.js's default export's fetch(request, env) takes plain Fetch API objects (Request/URL/Response are Node 18+ globals — no Cloudflare runtime needed) and env.ASSETS, an object with one method: fetch(request) -> Response. Test by constructing a request with `new Request('https://plant.minomobi.com/health')` and passing a stub `{ ASSETS: { fetch: async () => new Response(...) } }`:
  - ASSETS.fetch resolving with an ok Response (status 200) -> /health returns status 200, JSON body { ok: true, surface: 'plant', serves: 'index.html' }, and the three fixed headers (content-type application/json;charset=utf-8, access-control-allow-origin *, cache-control no-store) — assert each header individually, not just presence of a header object.
  - ASSETS.fetch resolving with a non-ok Response (e.g. status 404) -> /health returns status 503, body { ok: false, surface: 'plant', serves: null }.
  - ASSETS.fetch REJECTING (throws) -> caught, not propagated: /health still returns status 503 with the same ok:false/serves:null shape, proving the try/catch in worker.js's header comment ('reported, not thrown') actually holds.
  - ASSETS.fetch is called with a request whose URL path is /index.html on the ORIGINAL request's origin, regardless of what path the /health request itself came in on — capture the request worker.js hands to the stub's fetch and assert its .url ends in /index.html.
  - Pass-through: for any path other than /health (e.g. /foo.js), fetch(request, env) returns exactly what env.ASSETS.fetch(request) returned (identity-check via a marker Response object, not just an equivalent one) and is called with the ORIGINAL request object unchanged (identity-check, not a reconstructed one) — worker.js's fall-through line is `return env.ASSETS.fetch(request);` with no wrapping, and this is the assertion that a future edit doesn't quietly start rewrapping or cloning it.

Bounded paths: plant/worker.js (read only) and plant/test/worker.selftest.mjs (new). Independent of every open ticket (R4) — worker.js has no dependency on any in-flight change. Reversible (R6): a failed attempt is a new test file that either doesn't exist or is deleted; nothing else changes.

beads.body:
BOUNDED PATHS (R3): plant/test/worker.selftest.mjs only (new file). plant/worker.js is read, not modified — this ticket adds coverage for the file as it stands; if the test reveals worker.js itself needs a fix to pass, that is out of scope and should be a separate follow-up bead, not folded into this one.

WHY THIS ONE. plant/worker.js is the only server-side logic this surface has, and its whole reason for existing is CLAUDE.md's own principle: 'Green is not proof — verify the domain binding, the page, the endpoint.' Its /health branch is precisely the endpoint a human or a future turn would check to confirm a deploy actually worked (env.ASSETS.fetch('/index.html'), report ok/serves accordingly, status 200 vs 503). It has never had a test, in a repo whose own ledger records the exact failure mode this leaves open: 'the health probe failed for two minutes after the site was live — one missing space, masked by continue-on-error.' That finding was about a different surface's probe, but the lesson is general and worker.js's /health logic is untouched by any of plant/'s existing selftests (all of which exercise production.mjs / level-view.js / solids.mjs / view.js — nothing imports worker.js).

THE GATE — plant/test/worker.selftest.mjs, following this repo's plain-node, no-dependency, no-build-step house style (see plant/test/production.selftest.mjs's `ok()`/`failed` counter pattern). worker.js exports `export default { async fetch(request, env) {...} }`, so the test imports it directly (`import worker from '../worker.js'`) and calls `.fetch(request, env)` with a hand-built `env` object — no real Cloudflare runtime needed, since `env.ASSETS` is just an object with a `fetch` method the code calls once. Cases to cover, each a distinct assertion the current code must satisfy:
  1. GET /health when `env.ASSETS.fetch('/index.html')` resolves to a response with `.ok === true`: the worker's response has status 200, `content-type` includes `application/json`, and the parsed JSON body is exactly `{ ok: true, surface: 'plant', serves: 'index.html' }`.
  2. GET /health when `env.ASSETS.fetch(...)` resolves to a response with `.ok === false`: status 503, JSON body `{ ok: false, surface: 'plant', serves: null }`.
  3. GET /health when `env.ASSETS.fetch(...)` THROWS (simulate a binding failure): the worker does not itself throw — it catches, and behaves identically to case 2 (status 503, `ok: false, serves: null`). This is the one branch most likely to regress silently (the try/catch's empty-body comment says exactly 'index stays false — reported, not thrown').
  4. A non-/health path (e.g. GET /) is passed straight through: assert `env.ASSETS.fetch` is called with the original request and its return value is what the worker returns, unchanged — build a fake `env.ASSETS.fetch` that returns a distinguishable sentinel Response and assert the worker's return value is that same object (not a copy, not re-wrapped).
  5. Response headers on the /health path include `access-control-allow-origin: *` and `cache-control: no-store` in both the ok and not-ok cases (the two case branches share `HEALTH_HEADERS`, so this is one regression worth pinning explicitly rather than assuming from case 1/2).

R6 reversible: adds one new test file only, does not touch worker.js. R4 independent: no relationship to the CSS ticket above or to any other open bead — worker.js is untouched by every other test and every other currently-open ticket.

beads.title: Scoped the shared-sink autoSplit extension to a single-edge source-only 'other supplier'
beads.body: A sink fed by a fan-out group plus one outside edge only has an unambiguous, closed-form-solvable contribution from that outside edge when the outside supplier cannot itself be diluted by a fan-out or a processor's own scale calc — restricting it to a plain source with whole-network out-degree 1 keeps this a subtraction, not a second LP, and keeps the ticket inside one turn.

beads.title: Kept the new autoSplit ticket on a different qualifying condition than lp-9be387

Both edit autoSplit() but in physically separate parts of its predicate, so promoting both is expected to rebase cleanly rather than semantically conflict.

beads.title: Scoped feasible()'s new waste metric to output-side (unrouted share) only
beads.body: Input-side waste — a capacity-bound processor leaving supply it was offered but couldn't consume — needs tracking each input's offered-vs-used rate separately, a materially bigger change than reusing the existing per-edge share*emitted walk. Left alone this turn; output-side waste is a pure additive read of numbers the walk already computes.

beads.title: buildOrderLines() ships level-view.js-only, not wired into index.html or any level's DOM
beads.body: Same precedent as LEVEL_5 and LEVEL_6 both shipping their level module before a separate wiring ticket picked them up (lp-bc6980 and its LEVEL_6 counterpart) — keeps this ticket small and lets a later, independent ticket choose which level surfaces it without this one guessing.
